bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: __FORCETOC__
起昭陽大荒落，盡閼逢敦牂，凡二年。

translations.literal: From Zhaoyang Dahuanluo through Emao Dunzang; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhaoyang Dahuanluo through Emao Dunzang—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，泗川監平將兵圍沛公於豐，沛公出與戰，破之，令雍齒守豐。

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the tenth month, Sishui supervisor Ping led troops to besiege the Duke of Pei at Feng; the Duke of Pei came out to give battle, routed him, and ordered Yong Chi to hold Feng.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In the tenth month of winter, Sishui supervisor Ping besieged the Duke of Pei at Feng. The duke marched out, routed him, and left Yong Chi to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 十一月，沛公引兵之薛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Duke of Pei led his army to Xue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Duke of Pei marched on Xue.

sentences.zh: 泗川守壯兵敗於薛，走至戚，沛公左司馬得殺之。

translations.literal: Sishui grand administrator Zhuang was defeated at Xue, fled to Qi, and the Duke of Pei's Left Major was able to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The grand administrator of Sishui, Zhuang, was beaten at Xue and fled to Qi; the Duke of Pei's Left Major overtook and killed him.

sentences.zh: 2周章出關，止屯曹陽，二月餘，章邯追敗之。

translations.literal: 2. Zhou Zhang went out through the pass and halted at Caoyang for more than two months; Zhang Han pursued and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Zhou Zhang marched out through the pass and camped at Caoyang for more than two months before Zhang Han caught up and routed him.

sentences.zh: 復走澠池，十餘日，章邯擊，大破之。

translations.literal: He fled again to Mianchi; after more than ten days Zhang Han struck and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back on Mianchi; after a fortnight Zhang Han attacked and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 周文自刎，軍遂不戰。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen cut his own throat; the army then would not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen killed himself; his troops would fight no more.

sentences.zh: 吳叔圍滎陽，李由為三川守，守滎陽，叔弗能下。

translations.literal: Wu Shu besieged Xingyang; Li You was grand administrator of Sanchuan and held Xingyang; Shu could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shu besieged Xingyang. Li You, grand administrator of Sanchuan, held the city, and Shu could not bring it down.

sentences.zh: 楚將軍田臧等相與謀曰：「周章軍已破矣，秦兵旦暮至。

translations.literal: Chu general Tian Zang and others plotted together, saying: "Zhou Zhang's army is already broken; Qin troops will arrive any day now.
translations.idiomatic: Chu general Tian Zang and his officers took counsel: "Zhou Zhang's army is already destroyed. Qin will be here any day.

sentences.zh: 我圍滎陽城弗能下，秦兵至，必大敗，不如少遺兵守滎陽，悉精兵迎秦軍。

translations.literal: We besiege Xingyang and cannot take it; when Qin troops arrive we are sure to suffer a great defeat. Better to leave a few men to hold Xingyang and take all our picked troops to meet the Qin army.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot take Xingyang. When Qin comes we are finished. Better leave a skeleton force at the walls and march every able man to meet them.

sentences.zh: 今假王驕，不知兵權，不足與計事，恐敗。

translations.literal: Now the fake king is arrogant and does not understand the authority of arms; he is not fit to plan affairs with us—we fear defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The fake king is proud and knows nothing of command. He is no partner in counsel—we will lose everything.

sentences.zh: 」因相與矯王令以誅吳叔，獻其首於陳王。

translations.literal: " Thereupon together they forged the king's order to execute Wu Shu and presented his head to King Chen.
translations.idiomatic: " They forged a royal order, killed Wu Shu, and sent his head to King Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳王使使賜田臧楚令尹印，使為上將。

translations.literal: King Chen sent an envoy to grant Tian Zang the seal of Chu grand minister and appoint him supreme general.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen sent envoys with the seal of Chu grand minister and made Tian Zang supreme general.

sentences.zh: 田臧乃使諸將李歸等守滎陽，自以精兵西迎秦軍於敖倉，與戰。

translations.literal: Tian Zang then ordered the generals Li Gui and the rest to hold Xingyang; he himself with picked troops went west to meet the Qin army at Aocang and gave battle.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zang left Li Gui and the other generals at Xingyang and marched west with his best men to meet Qin at Aocang.

sentences.zh: 田臧死，軍破。

translations.literal: Tian Zang died; the army was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zang fell; his army was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 章邯進兵擊李歸等滎陽下，破之，李歸等死。

translations.literal: Zhang Han advanced to attack Li Gui and the rest below Xingyang, routed them, and Li Gui and the rest died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han pressed on, struck Li Gui and his fellows below Xingyang, broke them, and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 陽城人鄧說將兵居郯，章邯別將擊破之。

translations.literal: Deng Shuo of Yangcheng led troops stationed at Tan; a detached Qin general under Zhang Han routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shuo of Yangcheng held Tan with his troops; one of Zhang Han's lieutenants routed him.

sentences.zh: 銍人伍逢將兵居許，章邯擊破之。

translations.literal: Wu Feng of Zhi led troops stationed at Xu; Zhang Han routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Feng of Zhi held Xu; Zhang Han broke him there.

sentences.zh: 兩軍皆散，走陳，陳王誅鄧說。

translations.literal: Both armies scattered and fled to Chen; King Chen executed Deng Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Both hosts broke and fled to Chen. King Chen had Deng Shuo executed.

sentences.zh: 3二世數誚讓李斯：「居三公位，如何令盜如此！

translations.literal: 3. The Second Emperor repeatedly reproached Li Si: "You hold one of the Three Excellencies—how could you let bandits come to this!
translations.idiomatic: 3. The Second Emperor berated Li Si again and again: "You sit among the Three Excellencies—how did you let rebels run wild like this!

sentences.zh: 」李斯恐懼，重爵祿，不知所出，乃阿二世意，以書對曰：「夫賢主者，必能行督責之術者也。

translations.literal: " Li Si was afraid; he valued rank and salary and did not know what course to take, so he flattered the Second Emperor's mind and answered in a memorial: "A worthy ruler must be one who can practice the art of stern oversight and blame.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Si was terrified. Rank and emolument weighed on him; he saw no way out. He bent to the emperor's mood and wrote back: "A true sovereign must practice stern oversight and blame.

sentences.zh: 故申子曰『有天下而不恣睢，命之曰以天下為桎梏』者，無他焉，不能督責，而顧以其身勞於天下之民，若堯、禹然，故謂之桎梏也。

translations.literal: Hence Shenzi says, 'To have all under Heaven yet not act as one pleases—this is called taking all under Heaven as fetters'—there is nothing else to it: unable to practice stern oversight and blame, yet instead to weary one's person laboring for the people of all under Heaven like Yao and Yu—therefore it is called fetters.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Shenzi says: 'To hold the realm and yet not do as you please is to wear the world as shackles.' Nothing more: if you cannot oversee and blame, but instead wear yourself out for the people like Yao or Yu, the throne becomes a chain.

sentences.zh: 夫不能修申、韓之明術，行督責之道，專以天下自適也；

translations.literal: One who cannot cultivate the bright arts of Shenzi and Han Feizi and walk the way of stern oversight and blame, but devotes himself solely to suiting himself with all under Heaven—
translations.idiomatic: He who will not master Shen and Han's clear methods, who will not walk the path of oversight and blame, but seeks only his own ease across the realm—

sentences.zh: 而徒務苦形勞神，以身徇百姓，則是黔首之役，非畜天下者也，何足貴哉！

translations.literal: yet only strives to torment the body and weary the spirit, offering his person for the common people—that is the servant of the black-headed masses, not one who nurtures all under Heaven. What is there to honor in that!
translations.idiomatic: who only breaks his body and drains his mind to serve the masses is a slave to the people, not a shepherd of the realm. What honor is there in that?

sentences.zh: 故明主能行督責之術以獨斷於上，則權不在臣下，然後能滅仁義之塗，絕諫說之辯，犖然行恣睢之心，而莫之敢逆。

translations.literal: Therefore the enlightened ruler, able to practice the art of stern oversight and blame and decide alone above, keeps power from lying with his ministers; only then can he extinguish the path of benevolence and righteousness, cut off the arguments of remonstrance, and stride at will with a proud heart while none dare oppose.
translations.idiomatic: The enlightened ruler practices oversight and blame, decides alone above, and keeps power from his ministers. Then he can stamp out the road of benevolence, silence every remonstrance, and follow his whim without a soul daring to resist.

sentences.zh: 如此，群臣、百姓救過不給，何變之敢圖！

translations.literal: When it is so, ministers and common people have not enough to spare for correcting faults—how would they dare plot change!
translations.idiomatic: Then ministers and people will have no breath to spare for fault or plot—who would dare dream of rebellion?

sentences.zh: 」二世說，於是行督責益嚴，稅民深者為明吏，殺人眾者為忠臣，刑者相半於道，而死人日成積於市，秦民益駭懼思亂。

translations.literal: " The Second Emperor was pleased; thereupon oversight and blame grew stricter still. Those who taxed the people heavily were deemed enlightened officials; those who killed many were deemed loyal ministers. Half the road was lined with men under punishment, and corpses piled in the market day by day; the people of Qin grew ever more terrified and thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " The Second Emperor was delighted. Oversight and blame grew harsher still. Heavy taxers were called good officials; prolific executioners, loyal ministers. Half the highways were flogging-grounds; the markets filled with corpses day by day. Qin trembled—and dreamed of revolt.

sentences.zh: 4趙李良已定常山，還報趙王。

translations.literal: 4. Li Liang of Zhao had already pacified Changshan and returned to report to the king of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: 4. Li Liang of Zhao had pacified Changshan and returned to report to the king of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 趙王復使良略太原。

translations.literal: The king of Zhao again sent Liang to seize Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent him out again to take Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 至石邑，秦兵塞井陘，未能前。

translations.literal: When he reached Shiyi, Qin troops blocked Jingxing and he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: At Shiyi, Qin blocked the Jingxing pass; he could not advance.

sentences.zh: 秦將詐為二世書以招良。

translations.literal: A Qin general forged a letter in the Second Emperor's name to win Li Liang over.
translations.idiomatic: A Qin general forged a letter in the Second Emperor's name to win Li Liang over.

sentences.zh: 良得書未信，還之邯鄲，益請兵。

translations.literal: Li Liang received the letter but did not believe it; he returned to Handan and asked for more troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liang took the letter but did not trust it. He went back to Handan and asked for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 未至，道逢趙王姊出飲，從百餘騎，良望見，以為王，伏謁道旁。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he met the king of Zhao's elder sister going out to drink, with more than a hundred riders in attendance; Li Liang saw her from afar, took her for the king, and bowed prostrate by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met the king of Zhao's elder sister out drinking, with a hundred-odd riders. Li Liang mistook her for the king and bowed in the dust by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 王姊醉，不知其將，使騎謝李良。

translations.literal: The king's sister was drunk and did not know he was a general; she sent a rider to apologize to Li Liang.
translations.idiomatic: She was drunk and did not know he was a general. She sent a rider to apologize.

sentences.zh: 李良素貴，起，慚其從官。

translations.literal: Li Liang had always been honored; he rose, ashamed before his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liang had always held high rank. He rose, burning with shame before his men.

sentences.zh: 從官有一人曰：「天下畔秦，能者先立。

translations.literal: One of his attendants said: "All under Heaven rebels against Qin; the able man rises first.
translations.idiomatic: One attendant said: "The realm rebels against Qin. The able man rises first.

sentences.zh: 且趙王素出將軍下，今女兒乃不為將軍下車，請追殺之！

translations.literal: Moreover the king of Zhao has always ranked below you, the general; now this woman would not even step down from her carriage for you—please pursue and kill her!
translations.idiomatic: The king of Zhao has always ranked below you. Now his sister would not even step down from her carriage—pursue her and kill her!

sentences.zh: 」李良已得秦書，固欲反趙，未決，因此怒，遣人追殺王姊，因將其兵襲邯鄲。

translations.literal: " Li Liang had already received the Qin letter and had long wished to turn against Zhao but had not decided; stirred by this anger, he sent men to pursue and kill the king's sister, then led his troops to strike Handan.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Liang already held Qin's letter and had been weighing defection. This insult decided him. He sent men after the king's sister, killed her, and marched on Handan.

sentences.zh: 邯鄲不知，竟殺趙王、邵騷。

translations.literal: Handan did not know; in the end he killed the king of Zhao and Shao Sao.
translations.idiomatic: Handan was taken unawares. He killed the king of Zhao and Shao Sao.

sentences.zh: 趙人多為張耳、陳餘耳目者，以故二人獨得脫。

translations.literal: Many in Zhao served as Zhang Er's and Chen Yu's eyes and ears; for this reason the two alone escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Many in Zhao were Zhang Er's and Chen Yu's eyes and ears; for that the two alone escaped.

sentences.zh: 5陳人秦嘉、符離人朱雞石等起兵，圍東海守於郯。

translations.literal: 5. Qin Jia of Chen, Zhu Jishi of Fuli, and others raised troops and besieged the grand administrator of Donghai at Tan.
translations.idiomatic: 5. Qin Jia of Chen, Zhu Jishi of Fuli, and others rose and besieged the grand administrator of Donghai at Tan.

sentences.zh: 陳王聞之，使武平君畔為將軍，監郯下軍。

translations.literal: King Chen heard of it and sent Lord Wuping Pan as general to oversee the army below Tan.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen heard and sent Lord Wuping Pan as general to oversee the army at Tan.

sentences.zh: 秦嘉不受命，自立為大司馬，惡屬武平君，告軍吏曰：「武平君年少，不知兵事，勿聽！

translations.literal: Qin Jia would not accept the order; he declared himself Grand Marshal, detested being subordinate to Lord Wuping, and told the army officers: "Lord Wuping is young and does not understand military affairs—do not heed him!
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jia refused the order, declared himself Grand Marshal, and scorned serving under Lord Wuping. He told the officers: "Lord Wuping is young and knows nothing of war. Pay him no heed!

sentences.zh: 」因矯以王命殺武平君畔。

translations.literal: " He then forged the king's command and killed Lord Wuping Pan.
translations.idiomatic: " He forged a royal order and killed Lord Wuping Pan.

sentences.zh: 6二世益遣長史司馬欣、董翳佐章邯擊盜。

translations.literal: 6. The Second Emperor further sent chief clerks Sima Xin and Dong Yi to assist Zhang Han in attacking the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: 6. The Second Emperor sent chief clerks Sima Xin and Dong Yi to assist Zhang Han against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 章邯已破伍逢，擊陳柱國房君，殺之。

translations.literal: Zhang Han had already routed Wu Feng; he attacked Lord Fang, pillar of state of Chen, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han had already broken Wu Feng. He struck Lord Fang, pillar of state of Chen, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 又進擊陳西張賀軍。

translations.literal: He advanced again to attack Zhang He's army west of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed west against Zhang He's army.

sentences.zh: 陳王出監戰。

translations.literal: King Chen came out to oversee the battle.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen came out in person to oversee the fight.

sentences.zh: 張賀死。

translations.literal: Zhang He died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He fell.

sentences.zh: 7臘月，陳王之汝陰，還，至下城父，其御莊賈殺陳王以降。

translations.literal: 7. In the twelfth month King Chen went to Ruyin; on his return, when he reached Xiachengfu, his charioteer Zhuang Jia killed King Chen to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: 7. In the twelfth month King Chen went to Ruyin. On his return, at Xiachengfu, his charioteer Zhuang Jia killed him and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 初，陳涉既為王，其故人皆往依之。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Chen She became king, his old friends all came to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen She first became king, every old friend came to cling to him.

sentences.zh: 妻之父亦往焉，陳王以眾賓待之，長揖不拜。

translations.literal: His wife's father also came; King Chen received him among the many guests with a long bow but did not perform the full obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: His father-in-law came too. Chen treated him as one guest among many—a long bow, no full obeisance.

sentences.zh: 妻之父怒曰：「怙亂僭號，而傲長者，不能久矣！

translations.literal: His wife's father said in anger: "You rely on disorder to usurp a royal title, yet you are arrogant toward your elders—you cannot last!
translations.idiomatic: The father-in-law raged: "You ride rebellion to a royal title, yet scorn your elders—you will not last!"

sentences.zh: 」不辭而去。

translations.literal: " Without taking leave he departed.
translations.idiomatic: " He left without farewell.

sentences.zh: 陳王跪謝，遂不為顧。

translations.literal: King Chen knelt to apologize, but he would not look back.
translations.idiomatic: Chen knelt to apologize. The old man would not turn back.

sentences.zh: 客出入愈益發舒，言陳王故情。

translations.literal: Guests coming and going grew ever more unrestrained, speaking of King Chen's former circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Guests grew bolder at every visit, retailing Chen's old life in the fields.

sentences.zh: 或說陳王曰：「客愚無知，顓妄言，輕威。

translations.literal: Someone advised King Chen: "These guests are foolish and ignorant; they speak recklessly and lightly wound your majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him: "These guests are fools. Their loose tongues cheapen your majesty.

sentences.zh: 」陳王斬之。

translations.literal: " King Chen beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen had the man beheaded.

sentences.zh: 諸故人皆自引去，由是無親陳王者。

translations.literal: All his old friends withdrew of themselves; from this there were none close to King Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Every old friend slipped away. After that, none remained close to Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳王以朱防為中正，胡武為司過，主司群臣。

translations.literal: King Chen made Zhu Fang Director of the Center and Hu Wu Director of Faults, putting them in charge of overseeing the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Chen made Zhu Fang Director of the Center and Hu Wu Director of Faults to oversee his ministers.

sentences.zh: 諸將徇地至，令之不是，輒系而罪之。

translations.literal: When generals who had seized territory arrived, if their orders were not to his liking he would bind and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Generals returning from conquered lands were bound and punished if their reports displeased him.

sentences.zh: 以苛察為忠，其所不善者，弗下吏，輒自治之。

translations.literal: He took harsh scrutiny as loyalty; those he disliked he did not hand to the clerks but punished himself.
translations.idiomatic: He mistook harshness for loyalty. Those he disliked he punished himself, without troubling the clerks.

sentences.zh: 諸將以其故不親附，此其所以敗也。

translations.literal: The generals for this reason would not draw close to him—this is why he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The generals would not stand by him. That is why he fell.

sentences.zh: 陳王故涓人將軍呂臣為蒼頭軍，起新陽，攻陳，下之，殺莊賈，復以陳為楚。

translations.literal: King Chen's former palace attendant, General Lü Chen, raised the Servant Army at Xinyang, attacked Chen, took it, killed Zhuang Jia, and restored Chen as Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's old palace attendant, General Lü Chen, raised the Servant Army at Xinyang, retook Chen, killed Zhuang Jia, and made Chu of Chen again.

sentences.zh: 葬陳王於碭，謚曰隱王。

translations.literal: They buried King Chen at Dang and gave him the posthumous title Hidden King.
translations.idiomatic: They buried King Chen at Dang with the posthumous name Hidden King.

sentences.zh: 初，陳王令銍人宋留將兵定南陽，入武關。

translations.literal: Earlier King Chen had ordered Song Liu of Zhi to lead troops to pacify Nanyang and enter Wu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chen had ordered Song Liu of Zhi to pacify Nanyang and enter Wu Pass.

sentences.zh: 留已徇南陽，聞陳王死，南陽復為秦，宋留以軍降，二世車裂留以徇。

translations.literal: Liu had already seized Nanyang; when he heard King Chen was dead, Nanyang returned to Qin; Song Liu surrendered with his army; the Second Emperor had Liu torn apart by chariots as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu had taken Nanyang. When he heard Chen was dead, Nanyang went back to Qin. Song Liu surrendered with his army. The Second Emperor had him torn apart by chariots as a warning.

sentences.zh: 8魏周市將兵略地豐、沛，使人招雍齒。

translations.literal: 8. Zhou Shi of Wei led troops to seize the lands of Feng and Pei and sent someone to win over Yong Chi.
translations.idiomatic: 8. Zhou Shi of Wei marched to take Feng and Pei and sent to win over Yong Chi.

sentences.zh: 雍齒雅不欲屬沛公，即以豐降魏。

translations.literal: Yong Chi had never wished to belong to the Duke of Pei; he thereupon surrendered Feng to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Chi had never wished to serve the Duke of Pei. He surrendered Feng to Wei.

sentences.zh: 沛公攻之，不克。

translations.literal: The Duke of Pei attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Pei attacked and could not take it.

sentences.zh: 9趙張耳、陳餘收其散兵，得數萬人，擊李良。

translations.literal: 9. Zhang Er and Chen Yu of Zhao gathered their scattered troops, mustered several tens of thousands, and attacked Li Liang.
translations.idiomatic: 9. Zhang Er and Chen Yu of Zhao gathered their scattered men—several tens of thousands—and struck Li Liang.

sentences.zh: 良敗，走歸章邯。

translations.literal: Li Liang was defeated and fled back to Zhang Han.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liang was beaten and fled to Zhang Han.

sentences.zh: 客有說耳、餘曰：「兩君羈旅，而欲附趙，難可獨立。

translations.literal: A guest advised Zhang Er and Chen Yu: "You two are travelers in exile; you wish to attach yourselves to Zhao—it is hard to stand alone.
translations.idiomatic: A guest told Zhang Er and Chen Yu: "You are strangers in a strange land, clinging to Zhao. You cannot stand alone.

sentences.zh: 立趙後，輔以誼，可就功。

translations.literal: Establish a descendant of Zhao and assist him with righteousness, and you may achieve your aim.
translations.idiomatic: Set up a scion of Zhao, serve him with loyalty, and you may win through.

sentences.zh: 」乃求得趙歇。

translations.literal: " They then sought out and found Zhao Xie.
translations.idiomatic: " They found Zhao Xie.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，耳、餘立歇為趙王，居信都。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Zhang Er and Chen Yu established Xie as king of Zhao and dwelt at Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring they made Xie king of Zhao and held court at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 10東陽寧君、秦嘉聞陳王軍敗，乃立景駒為楚王，引兵之方與，欲擊秦軍定陶下；

translations.literal: 10. Ning Jun of Dongyang and Qin Jia, hearing King Chen's army was defeated, thereupon established Jing Ju as king of Chu, led troops to Fangyu, and meant to strike the Qin army below Dingtao;
translations.idiomatic: 10. Ning Jun of Dongyang and Qin Jia, hearing Chen's army was broken, made Jing Ju king of Chu, marched to Fangyu, and meant to strike Qin below Dingtao;

sentences.zh: 使公孫慶使齊，欲與之並力俱進。

translations.literal: they sent Gongsun Qing as envoy to Qi, wishing to join forces and advance together.
translations.idiomatic: they sent Gongsun Qing to Qi to join forces and advance together.

sentences.zh: 齊王曰：「陳王戰敗，不知其死生，楚安得不請而立王！

translations.literal: The king of Qi said: "King Chen was defeated in battle; we do not know whether he lives or dies—how can Chu not ask permission before establishing a king!
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi said: "Chen was beaten in battle. We do not know if he lives. How dare Chu set up a king without asking us!

sentences.zh: 」公孫慶曰：「齊不請楚而立王，楚何故請齊而立王！

translations.literal: " Gongsun Qing said: "Qi did not ask Chu before establishing a king—why should Chu ask Qi before establishing a king!
translations.idiomatic: " Gongsun Qing said: "Qi never asked Chu before making a king. Why should Chu ask Qi?

sentences.zh: 且楚首事，當令於天下。

translations.literal: Moreover Chu was first in the affair; it ought to give orders to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Chu rose first. Chu ought to give orders under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」田儋殺公孫慶。

translations.literal: " Tian Dan killed Gongsun Qing.
translations.idiomatic: " Tian Dan killed Gongsun Qing.

sentences.zh: 11秦左、右校復攻陳，下之。

translations.literal: 11. The Qin Left and Right Commandants again attacked Chen and took it.
translations.idiomatic: 11. Qin's Left and Right Commandants attacked Chen again and took it.

sentences.zh: 呂將軍走，徼兵復聚，與番盜黥布相遇，攻擊秦左、右校，破之青波，復以陳為楚。

translations.literal: General Lü fled; he gathered scattered troops again, met the bandit of Fan, Qing Bu, attacked the Qin Left and Right Commandants, routed them at Qingbo, and restored Chen as Chu.
translations.idiomatic: General Lü fled, rallied his scattered men, met the bandit lord of Fan, Qing Bu, struck the Left and Right Commandants, broke them at Qingbo, and made Chu of Chen once more.

sentences.zh: 黥布者，六人也，姓英氏，坐法黥，以刑徒論輸驪山。

translations.literal: Qing Bu was a man of Liu, surname Ying; convicted by law he was tattooed and, as a penal laborer, was sent to work at Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Bu was from Liu, of the Ying clan. Convicted, he was tattooed and sent as a convict laborer to Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 驪山之徒數十萬人，布皆與其徒長豪傑交通，乃率其曹耦，亡之江中為群盜。

translations.literal: The laborers at Mount Li numbered several hundred thousand; Bu associated with all the gang leaders and great men among them, then led his fellows and fled to the Yangtze to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands labored at Mount Li. Bu made common cause with every gang leader and strong man there, then led his band south to the Yangtze and became a river pirate.

sentences.zh: 番陽令吳芮，甚得江湖間心，號曰番君。

translations.literal: Wu Rui, magistrate of Poyang, won great hearts among those of the rivers and lakes; he was called Lord of Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Rui, magistrate of Poyang, held the loyalty of the river world and was called Lord of Fan.

sentences.zh: 布往見之，其眾已數千人。

translations.literal: Bu went to see him; his following already numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Bu went to him with several thousand men at his back.

sentences.zh: 番君乃以女妻之，使將其兵擊秦。

translations.literal: Lord of Fan then gave him his daughter in marriage and had him lead the troops against Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Lord of Fan gave him his daughter in marriage and set him at the head of the army against Qin.

sentences.zh: 12楚王景駒在留，沛公往從之。

translations.literal: 12. King Jing Ju of Chu was at Liu; the Duke of Pei went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: 12. King Jing Ju of Chu held Liu. The Duke of Pei went to join him.

sentences.zh: 張良亦聚少年百餘人，欲往從景駒，道遇沛公，遂屬焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang also gathered more than a hundred young men and meant to join Jing Ju; on the road he met the Duke of Pei and thereupon attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang too had gathered a hundred-odd youths and was bound for Jing Ju. On the road he met the Duke of Pei and attached himself to him instead.

sentences.zh: 沛公拜良為廄將。

translations.literal: The Duke of Pei appointed Zhang Liang Stable General.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Pei made Zhang Liang Stable General.

sentences.zh: 良數以太公兵法說沛公，沛公善之，常用其策。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang repeatedly expounded the Grand Duke's Art of War to the Duke of Pei; the duke was pleased with it and often used his stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang spoke again and again from the Grand Duke's Art of War. The duke delighted in it and often followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 良為他人言，皆不省。

translations.literal: When Zhang Liang spoke to others, none understood.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Liang spoke to anyone else, none understood.

sentences.zh: 良曰：「沛公殆天授！

translations.literal: Zhang Liang said: "The Duke of Pei is perhaps Heaven's gift!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang said: "The Duke of Pei is Heaven's chosen!

sentences.zh: 」故遂從不去。

translations.literal: " Therefore he followed and did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: " So he followed and never left.

sentences.zh: 沛公與良俱見景駒，欲請兵以攻豐。

translations.literal: The Duke of Pei and Zhang Liang together went to see Jing Ju and wished to ask for troops to attack Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Pei and Zhang Liang went together to Jing Ju and asked for troops to retake Feng.

sentences.zh: 時章邯司馬屍二將兵北定楚地，屠相，至碭。

translations.literal: At that time the Qin general under Zhang Han, Marshal Shi the Second, was leading troops north to pacify Chu territory; he slaughtered Xiang and reached Dang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhang Han's marshal, Shi the Second, was marching north to pacify Chu, sacked Xiang, and reached Dang.

sentences.zh: 東陽寧君、沛公引兵西，戰蕭西，不利，還，收兵聚留。

translations.literal: Ning Jun of Dongyang and the Duke of Pei led troops west, fought west of Xiao, met ill fortune, withdrew, and gathered their forces at Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Jun of Dongyang and the Duke of Pei marched west, fought west of Xiao, were beaten, fell back, and rallied at Liu.

sentences.zh: 二月，攻碭，三日，拔之。

translations.literal: In the second month, he attacked Dang; in three days he took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, he attacked Dang; in three days he took it.

sentences.zh: 收碭兵得六千人，與故合九千人。

translations.literal: Gathering the troops of Dang, he obtained six thousand men; with the former force combined, nine thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered six thousand troops from Dang; together with his existing force, he had nine thousand men.

sentences.zh: 三月，攻下邑，拔之。

translations.literal: In the third month, he attacked Xiayi and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, he attacked Xiayi and captured it.

sentences.zh: 還擊豐，不下。

translations.literal: Returning, he attacked Feng but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back to attack Feng but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 13廣陵人召平為陳王徇廣陵，未下。

translations.literal: 13. Zhao Ping of Guangling campaigned for the King of Chen against Guangling; he had not taken it.
translations.idiomatic: 13. Zhao Ping of Guangling was campaigning for King Chen against Guangling but had not yet captured it.

sentences.zh: 聞陳王敗走，章邯且至，乃渡江，矯陳王令，拜項梁為楚上柱國，曰：「江東已定，急引兵西擊秦！

translations.literal: Hearing that the King of Chen had been defeated and fled, and that Zhang Han was about to arrive, he crossed the Yangzi, forged an order in the King of Chen’s name, and appointed Xiang Liang Grand Pillar of State of Chu, saying: “The lands east of the river are already settled—hasten to lead your troops west to strike Qin!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that King Chen had been defeated and was fleeing, and that Zhang Han was approaching, he crossed the Yangzi, forged an order in King Chen’s name, and appointed Xiang Liang Grand Pillar of State of Chu, saying: “The lands east of the Yangzi are settled—lead your troops west at once to attack Qin!

sentences.zh: 」梁乃以八千人渡江而西。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Liang crossed the river westward with eight thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liang then crossed the river westward with eight thousand men.

sentences.zh: 聞陳嬰已下東陽，使使欲與連和俱西。

translations.literal: Hearing that Chen Ying had already taken Dongyang, he sent envoys wishing to join forces and go west together.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Chen Ying had already captured Dongyang, he sent envoys to propose a joint advance west.

sentences.zh: 陳嬰者，故東陽令史，居縣中，素信謹，稱為長者。

translations.literal: Chen Ying had been a clerk under the magistrate of Dongyang; living in the district, he was by nature trustworthy and careful, and was called an elder.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ying had been a clerk to the magistrate of Dongyang; living in the county seat, he was known for trustworthiness and prudence and was called an elder.

sentences.zh: 東陽少年殺其令，相聚得二萬人，欲立嬰為王。

translations.literal: The young men of Dongyang killed their magistrate, gathered together twenty thousand men, and wished to make Ying king.
translations.idiomatic: The young men of Dongyang killed their magistrate, gathered twenty thousand men, and wished to make Ying their king.

sentences.zh: 嬰母謂嬰曰：「自我為汝家婦，未嘗聞汝先世之有貴者。

translations.literal: Ying’s mother said to Ying: “Since I became your family’s daughter-in-law, I have never heard that any of your forebears attained high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ying’s mother said to him: “Since I married into your family, I have never heard of any distinguished ancestor among your forebears.

sentences.zh: 今暴得大名，不祥；

translations.literal: Now to obtain great fame suddenly is inauspicious;
translations.idiomatic: To rise suddenly to great fame is ill-omened;

sentences.zh: 不如有所屬。

translations.literal: it would be better to attach yourself to someone.
translations.idiomatic: it is better to place yourself under someone else’s leadership.

sentences.zh: 事成，猶得封侯；

translations.literal: If affairs succeed, you may still be enfeoffed as a marquis;
translations.idiomatic: If things succeed, you may still be enfeoffed as a marquis;

sentences.zh: 事敗，易以亡，非世所指名也。

translations.literal: if they fail, you can easily escape—unlike one whose name the age points at.
translations.idiomatic: if they fail, you can escape easily—you will not be the name the world singles out.

sentences.zh: 」嬰乃不敢為王，謂其軍吏曰：「項氏世世將家，有名於楚，今欲舉大事，將非其人不可。

translations.literal: ” Ying then dared not become king and said to his officers: “The Xiang clan for generations has been a military house, famous in Chu; now, wishing to undertake a great enterprise, one cannot do without the right commander.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ying then dared not become king and told his officers: “The Xiang clan has been a military house for generations, famous in Chu; to undertake a great enterprise now, we must have the right commander.

sentences.zh: 我倚名族，亡秦必矣！

translations.literal: If I rely on a renowned clan, the destruction of Qin is assured!”
translations.idiomatic: If I rely on a great house, Qin’s destruction is assured!”

sentences.zh: 」其眾從之，乃以兵屬梁。

translations.literal: ” His troops assented; he thereupon submitted his forces to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: ” His troops agreed, and he submitted his forces to Liang.

sentences.zh: 14英布既破秦軍，引兵而東；

translations.literal: 14. Ying Bu, having already defeated the Qin army, led his troops east;
translations.idiomatic: 14. After Ying Bu had defeated the Qin army, he led his troops east;

sentences.zh: 聞項梁西渡淮，布與蒲將軍皆以其兵屬焉。

translations.literal: hearing that Xiang Liang had crossed the Huai westward, Bu and General Pu both submitted their troops to him.
translations.idiomatic: hearing that Xiang Liang had crossed the Huai westward, Bu and General Pu both placed their troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 項梁眾凡六七萬人，軍下邳。

translations.literal: Xiang Liang’s forces totaled some sixty or seventy thousand men; he encamped at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Liang’s forces totaled some sixty or seventy thousand men; he encamped at Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 景駒、秦嘉軍彭城東，欲以距梁。

translations.literal: Jing Ju and Qin Jia encamped east of Pengcheng, intending to resist Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Ju and Qin Jia encamped east of Pengcheng, intending to block Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁謂軍吏曰：「陳王先首事，戰不利，未聞所在。

translations.literal: Liang said to his officers: “The King of Chen first raised the standard; the fighting went badly, and we have not heard where he is.
translations.idiomatic: Liang told his officers: “King Chen was first to raise the revolt; the fighting went badly, and we do not know where he is.

sentences.zh: 今秦嘉倍陳王而立景駒，逆無道！

translations.literal: Now Qin Jia has turned against the King of Chen and enthroned Jing Ju—rebellious and against the Way!”
translations.idiomatic: Now Qin Jia has betrayed King Chen and enthroned Jing Ju—this is treason!”

sentences.zh: 」乃進兵擊秦嘉，秦嘉軍敗走。

translations.literal: ” He thereupon advanced to attack Qin Jia; Qin Jia’s army was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: ” He advanced to attack Qin Jia; Qin Jia’s army was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 追之，至胡陵，嘉還戰。

translations.literal: Pursuing them to Huling, Jia turned to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing them to Huling, Jia turned to fight.

sentences.zh: 一日，嘉死，軍降；

translations.literal: In one day Jia died and the army surrendered;
translations.idiomatic: In a single day Jia was killed and his army surrendered;

sentences.zh: 景駒走死梁地。

translations.literal: Jing Ju fled and died in Liang’s territory.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Ju fled and was killed in Liang’s territory.

sentences.zh: 梁已並秦嘉軍，軍胡陵，將引軍而西。

translations.literal: Liang, having already absorbed Qin Jia’s army, encamped at Huling and was about to lead his troops west.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had absorbed Qin Jia’s army, encamped at Huling, and was preparing to march west.

sentences.zh: 章邯軍至栗，項梁使別將朱雞石、餘樊君與戰。

translations.literal: Zhang Han’s army reached Li; Xiang Liang sent the separate generals Zhu Jishi and Yu Fanjun to engage them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Han’s army reached Li, Xiang Liang sent the detached generals Zhu Jishi and Yu Fanjun to fight them.

sentences.zh: 餘樊君死，朱雞石軍敗，亡走胡陵。

translations.literal: Yu Fanjun died; Zhu Jishi’s army was defeated and fled to Huling.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fanjun was killed; Zhu Jishi’s army was defeated and fled to Huling.

sentences.zh: 梁乃引兵入薛，誅朱雞石。

translations.literal: Liang then led his troops into Xue and executed Zhu Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then marched into Xue and executed Zhu Jishi.

sentences.zh: 沛公從騎百餘往見梁，梁與沛公卒五千人，五大夫將十人。

translations.literal: The Lord of Pei went with a little over a hundred horsemen to see Liang; Liang gave the Lord of Pei five thousand foot soldiers and ten commanders of the fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Pei went with a little over a hundred horsemen to see Liang; Liang gave him five thousand infantry and ten commanders of the fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 沛公還，引兵攻豐，拔之。

translations.literal: The Lord of Pei returned, led his troops to attack Feng, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Pei returned, led his troops against Feng, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 雍齒奔魏。

translations.literal: Yong Chi fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Chi fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 項梁使項羽別攻襄城，襄城堅守不下；

translations.literal: Xiang Liang sent Xiang Yu on a separate mission to attack Xiangcheng; Xiangcheng held firm and could not be taken;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Liang sent Xiang Yu on a separate mission to attack Xiangcheng; the city held firm and would not fall;

sentences.zh: 已拔，皆坑之，還報。

translations.literal: once it was taken, he buried all alive in pits and returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: once it fell, he buried the defenders alive and returned to report.

sentences.zh: 梁聞陳王定死，召諸別將會薛計事，沛公亦往焉。

translations.literal: Liang, hearing that the King of Chen was certainly dead, summoned the various detached generals to meet at Xue to deliberate; the Lord of Pei also went.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that King Chen was certainly dead, Liang summoned the detached generals to a council at Xue; the Lord of Pei went as well.

sentences.zh: 居鄛人范增，年七十，素居家，好奇計，往說項梁曰：「陳勝敗，固當。

translations.literal: Fan Zeng of Juqi, seventy years old, had long lived at home and delighted in ingenious stratagems; he went to advise Xiang Liang, saying: “Chen Sheng’s defeat was bound to happen.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zeng of Juqi, seventy years old, had long lived in retirement and delighted in clever stratagems; he went to advise Xiang Liang: “Chen Sheng’s defeat was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 夫秦滅六國，楚最無罪。

translations.literal: When Qin destroyed the Six States, Chu was the most innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Six States Qin destroyed, Chu was the most blameless.

sentences.zh: 自懷王入秦不反，楚人憐之至今。

translations.literal: From the time King Huai entered Qin and did not return, the people of Chu have pitied him to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since King Huai entered Qin and never returned, the people of Chu have pitied him to this day.

sentences.zh: 故楚南公曰：『楚雖三戶，亡秦必楚。

translations.literal: Therefore Lord Nan of Chu said: ‘Though Chu has but three clans, it will be Chu that destroys Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Lord Nan of Chu said: ‘Though Chu has but three households, it will be Chu that destroys Qin.

sentences.zh: 』今陳勝首事，不立楚後而自立，其勢不長。

translations.literal: ’ Now Chen Sheng was first to raise the revolt yet did not establish a descendant of Chu and made himself ruler—such a position cannot last.
translations.idiomatic: ’ Chen Sheng was first to raise the revolt yet did not restore a descendant of Chu and made himself ruler—such power cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 今君起江東，楚蜂起之將皆爭附君者，以君世世楚將，為能復立楚之後也。

translations.literal: Now you have risen east of the river; the generals of Chu who have swarmed up like bees all vie to attach themselves to you because you are a Chu general for generations and can restore a descendant of Chu.”
translations.idiomatic: You have risen east of the Yangzi; the Chu commanders who have sprung up everywhere flock to you because you are a Chu general for generations and can restore a descendant of Chu.”

sentences.zh: 」於是項梁然其言，乃求得楚懷王孫心於民間，為人牧羊。

translations.literal: ” Xiang Liang thereupon approved his words and sought out Xin, grandson of King Huai of Chu, among the people—he was tending sheep.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xiang Liang agreed and found Xin, grandson of King Huai of Chu, among the people—he had been tending sheep.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，立以為楚懷王，從民望也。

translations.literal: in summer, the sixth month, established him as King Huai of Chu, following the people’s hopes.
translations.idiomatic: in summer, the sixth month, enthroned him as King Huai of Chu, to satisfy popular expectation.

sentences.zh: 陳嬰為上柱國，封五縣，與懷王都盱眙。

translations.literal: Chen Ying became Grand Pillar of State, was enfeoffed with five districts, and together with King Huai made his capital at Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ying became Grand Pillar of State, received five districts as his fief, and joined King Huai at the capital in Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 項梁自號為武信君。

translations.literal: Xiang Liang styled himself Lord Martial and Faithful.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Liang styled himself Lord Martial and Faithful.

sentences.zh: 張良說項梁曰：「君已立楚後，而韓諸公子橫陽君成最賢，可立為王，益樹黨。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang advised Xiang Liang: “Your Lordship has already established a descendant of Chu; among the princes of Han, Cheng, Lord of Hengyang, is the most worthy and may be enthroned as king—this will further plant allies.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang urged Xiang Liang: “You have already restored Chu’s royal line; among Han’s princes, Cheng, Lord of Hengyang, is the worthiest and should be made king—this will strengthen your party.”

sentences.zh: 」項梁使良求韓成，立以為韓王，以良為司徒，與韓王將千餘人西略韓地，得數城，秦輒復取之；

translations.literal: ” Xiang Liang sent Liang to find Han Cheng, established him as King of Han, made Liang Minister over the Masses, and with the King of Han and a little over a thousand troops campaigned west into Han territory, taking several cities—Qin then recovered them again;
translations.idiomatic: ” Xiang Liang sent Zhang Liang to find Han Cheng, enthroned him as King of Han, made Zhang Liang Minister over the Masses, and with the King of Han and a little over a thousand men campaigned west into Han territory, capturing several cities that Qin soon recaptured;

sentences.zh: 往來為遊兵穎川。

translations.literal: they went back and forth as roving troops in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: they ranged back and forth as roving troops in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 15章邯已破陳王，乃進兵擊魏王於臨濟。

translations.literal: 15. Zhang Han, having already defeated the King of Chen, then advanced to attack the King of Wei at Linji.
translations.idiomatic: 15. After Zhang Han had defeated King Chen, he advanced to attack the King of Wei at Linji.

sentences.zh: 魏王使周市出，請救於齊、楚。

translations.literal: The King of Wei sent Zhou Shi out to request aid from Qi and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wei sent Zhou Shi to seek aid from Qi and Chu.

sentences.zh: 齊王儋及楚將項它皆將兵隨市救魏。

translations.literal: King Dan of Qi and the Chu general Xiang Ta both led troops following Shi to rescue Wei.
translations.idiomatic: King Dan of Qi and the Chu general Xiang Ta both led troops with Zhou Shi to rescue Wei.

sentences.zh: 章邯夜銜枚擊，大破齊、楚軍於臨濟下，殺齊王及周市。

translations.literal: Zhang Han attacked by night with gags in the men’s mouths, greatly defeated the Qi and Chu armies below Linji, and killed the King of Qi and Zhou Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han attacked by night with gags in the soldiers’ mouths, routed the Qi and Chu armies below Linji, and killed the King of Qi and Zhou Shi.

sentences.zh: 魏王咎為其民約降，約定，自燒殺。

translations.literal: King Jiu of Wei made a surrender pact for his people’s sake; when the terms were set, he burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: King Jiu of Wei negotiated surrender for his people’s sake; when terms were agreed, he burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 其弟豹亡走楚，楚懷王予魏豹數千人，復徇魏地。

translations.literal: His younger brother Bao fled to Chu; King Huai of Chu gave Wei Bao several thousand men, and he campaigned again through Wei territory.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Bao fled to Chu; King Huai gave Wei Bao several thousand men, and he campaigned again through Wei territory.

sentences.zh: 齊田榮收其兄儋餘兵，東走東阿，章邯追圍之。

translations.literal: Tian Rong of Qi gathered his elder brother Dan’s remaining troops, fled east to Dong’e, and Zhang Han pursued and besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong of Qi gathered his brother Dan’s remaining troops, fled east to Dong’e, and Zhang Han pursued and besieged him.

sentences.zh: 齊人聞齊王儋死，乃立故齊王建之弟假為王，田角為相，角弟間為將，以距諸侯。

translations.literal: The people of Qi, hearing that King Dan of Qi was dead, thereupon enthroned Jia, younger brother of the former King Jian of Qi, as king; Tian Jiao became chancellor, and Jiao’s younger brother Jian became general, to resist the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Qi heard that King Dan was dead, they enthroned Jia, younger brother of the former King Jian of Qi; Tian Jiao became chancellor and Jiao’s younger brother Jian became general, to resist the allied lords.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，大霖雨。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, there were great torrential rains.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, there were torrential rains.

sentences.zh: 武信君引兵攻亢父，聞田榮之急，乃引兵擊破章邯軍東阿下，章邯走而西。

translations.literal: Lord Martial and Faithful led his troops to attack Kangfu; hearing that Tian Rong was in peril, he turned his troops and defeated Zhang Han’s army below Dong’e; Zhang Han fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Martial and Faithful marched to attack Kangfu; hearing that Tian Rong was in peril, he turned and defeated Zhang Han’s army below Dong’e; Zhang Han fled west.

sentences.zh: 田榮引兵東歸齊。

translations.literal: Tian Rong led his troops east back to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong led his troops east back into Qi.

sentences.zh: 武信君獨追北，使項羽、沛公別攻城陽，屠之。

translations.literal: Lord Martial and Faithful alone pursued north; he sent Xiang Yu and the Lord of Pei on separate missions to attack Chengyang and slaughtered it.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Martial and Faithful alone pursued north; he sent Xiang Yu and the Lord of Pei on separate missions to attack Chengyang and put it to the sword.

sentences.zh: 楚軍軍濮陽東，復與章邯戰，又破之。

translations.literal: The Chu army encamped east of Puyang, fought Zhang Han again, and defeated him once more.
translations.idiomatic: The Chu army encamped east of Puyang, fought Zhang Han again, and defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 章邯復振，守濮陽，環水。

translations.literal: Zhang Han recovered his strength, held Puyang, and ringed it with water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han rallied, held Puyang, and ringed it with moats.

sentences.zh: 沛公、項羽去，攻定陶。

translations.literal: The Lord of Pei and Xiang Yu departed and attacked Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Pei and Xiang Yu left and attacked Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 八月，田榮擊逐齊王假，假亡走楚，田角亡走趙。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Tian Rong attacked and drove out King Jia of Qi; Jia fled to Chu, and Tian Jiao fled to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Tian Rong attacked and drove out King Jia of Qi; Jia fled to Chu and Tian Jiao fled to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 田間前救趙，因留不敢歸。

translations.literal: Tian Jian had earlier gone to rescue Zhao and therefore stayed on, not daring to return.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jian had earlier gone to aid Zhao and therefore stayed there, not daring to return.

sentences.zh: 田榮乃立儋子市為齊王，榮相之，田橫為將，平齊地。

translations.literal: Tian Rong thereupon enthroned Dan’s son Shi as King of Qi; Rong became his chancellor, Tian Heng became general, and they pacified Qi territory.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong enthroned Dan’s son Shi as King of Qi; Rong became chancellor, Tian Heng became general, and they pacified Qi.

sentences.zh: 章邯兵益盛，項梁數使使告齊、趙發兵共擊章邯。

translations.literal: Zhang Han’s troops grew ever stronger; Xiang Liang repeatedly sent envoys urging Qi and Zhao to raise troops and join in attacking Zhang Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han’s forces grew stronger; Xiang Liang repeatedly sent envoys urging Qi and Zhao to raise troops and join him against Zhang Han.

sentences.zh: 田榮曰：「楚殺田假，趙殺角、間，乃出兵。

translations.literal: Tian Rong said: “If Chu kills Tian Jia and Zhao kills Jiao and Jian, then I will send troops.”
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong said: “If Chu kills Tian Jia and Zhao kills Jiao and Jian, then I will send troops.”

sentences.zh: 」楚、趙不許。

translations.literal: ” Chu and Zhao would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chu and Zhao refused.

sentences.zh: 田榮怒，終不肯出兵。

translations.literal: Tian Rong was angry and in the end refused to send troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong was enraged and in the end refused to send troops.

sentences.zh: 16郎中令趙高恃恩專恣，以私怨誅殺人眾多，恐大臣入朝奏事言之，乃說二世曰：「天子之所以貴者，但以聞聲，群臣莫得見其面故也。

translations.literal: 16. Zhao Gao, Director of the Palace, relied on favor and acted arbitrarily; because of private grudges he put many to death. Fearing that when great ministers came to court to report affairs they would speak of this, he persuaded the Second Emperor, saying: “The reason the Son of Heaven is held august is simply that men hear his voice while the ministers cannot see his face.
translations.idiomatic: 16. Zhao Gao, Director of the Palace, relied on imperial favor and acted arbitrarily; he executed many people over private grudges. Fearing that ministers reporting at court would speak of this, he persuaded the Second Emperor: “The Son of Heaven is held august because men hear his voice while ministers cannot see his face.

sentences.zh: 且陛下富於春秋，未必盡通諸事。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty is still young in years and may not yet be fully versed in all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty is still young and may not yet understand all affairs thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 今坐朝廷，譴舉有不當者，則見短於大臣，非所以示神明於天下也。

translations.literal: Now to sit in court—if in reproof or recommendation something is improper, you will be exposed as deficient before the great ministers; this is not the way to display numinous clarity to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If you sit in court now and your rebukes or recommendations are ever improper, you will be exposed before the ministers—this is not how to display divine wisdom to the realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下不如深拱禁中，與臣及侍中習法者待事，事來有以揆之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty would do better to withdraw deep within the inner palace, and with me and the attendants-in-ordinary who are versed in law await affairs; when matters come, there will be means to measure them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty would do better to withdraw deep into the inner palace; with me and the attendants-in-ordinary versed in law you can await business and weigh each matter as it comes.

sentences.zh: 如此，則大臣不敢奏疑事，天下稱聖主矣。

translations.literal: In this way the great ministers will not dare present doubtful matters, and all under Heaven will call you a sage ruler.”
translations.idiomatic: Then ministers will not dare present doubtful matters, and the realm will call you a sage ruler.”

sentences.zh: 」二世用其計，乃不坐朝廷見大臣，常居禁中。

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor adopted his plan, ceased to sit in court and see the great ministers, and constantly dwelt within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor adopted his plan, stopped holding court and seeing ministers, and constantly remained in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 趙高侍中用事，事皆決於趙高。

translations.literal: Zhao Gao, as attendant-in-ordinary, held power; all affairs were decided by Zhao Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao held power as attendant-in-ordinary; all affairs were decided by Zhao Gao.

sentences.zh: 高聞李斯以為言，乃見丞相曰：「關東群盜多，今上急，益發繇，治阿房宮，聚狗馬無用之物。

translations.literal: Gao heard that Li Si was speaking about this and thereupon saw the chancellor, saying: “The bandits east of the passes are many; the present emperor is in haste, yet increases corvée labor, builds Epang Palace, and gathers useless things like dogs and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Gao heard that Li Si was speaking of this and went to the chancellor: “Bandits east of the passes are numerous; the emperor is in distress, yet corvée is increased, Epang Palace is being built, and useless things like dogs and horses are gathered.

sentences.zh: 臣欲諫，為位賤，此真君侯之事。

translations.literal: I wish to remonstrate, but my rank is low—this is truly the lord chancellor’s affair.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to remonstrate, but my rank is too low—this is truly your affair, my lord.

sentences.zh: 君何不諫？

translations.literal: Why does my lord not remonstrate?”
translations.idiomatic: Why do you not remonstrate?”

sentences.zh: 」李斯曰：「固也，吾欲言之久矣。

translations.literal: ” Li Si said: “Indeed—I have long wished to speak.
translations.idiomatic: ” Li Si said: “Indeed—I have long wished to speak.

sentences.zh: 今時上不坐朝廷，常居深宮。

translations.literal: Now the emperor does not sit in court but constantly dwells in the deep palace.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor does not hold court but constantly dwells deep in the palace.

sentences.zh: 吾所言者，不可傳也。

translations.literal: What I would say cannot be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: What I would say cannot be relayed by others.

sentences.zh: 欲見，無閒。

translations.literal: I wish to see him but have no leisure.”
translations.idiomatic: I wish to see him but have no opportunity.”

sentences.zh: 」趙高曰：「君誠能諫，請為君侯上閒，語君。

translations.literal: ” Zhao Gao said: “If my lord truly can remonstrate, please let me secure leisure for you with the lord chancellor and inform you.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhao Gao said: “If you truly wish to remonstrate, let me secure an audience for you and inform you.”

sentences.zh: 」於是趙高待二世方燕樂，婦女居前，使人告丞相：「上方閒，可奏事。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Zhao Gao waited until the Second Emperor was at ease feasting, with women placed before him, and sent word to the chancellor: “His Majesty has leisure; you may report affairs.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhao Gao waited until the Second Emperor was feasting at leisure with women before him, then sent word to the chancellor: “His Majesty has leisure; you may report.”

sentences.zh: 」丞相至宮門上謁。

translations.literal: ” The chancellor came to the palace gate and presented himself.
translations.idiomatic: ” The chancellor came to the palace gate and requested audience.

sentences.zh: 如此者三。

translations.literal: This happened three times.
translations.idiomatic: This happened three times.

sentences.zh: 二世怒曰：「吾常多閒日，丞相不來；

translations.literal: The Second Emperor said angrily: “I often have much leisure, yet the chancellor does not come;
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor said angrily: “I often have much leisure, yet the chancellor does not come;

sentences.zh: 吾方燕私，丞相輒來請事！

translations.literal: just when I am privately feasting at ease, the chancellor repeatedly comes to request an audience!
translations.idiomatic: just when I am privately feasting, the chancellor keeps coming to report!

sentences.zh: 丞相豈少我哉，且固我哉？

translations.literal: Does the chancellor think little of me, or is he trying to constrain me?”
translations.idiomatic: Does the chancellor despise me, or is he trying to constrain me?”

sentences.zh: 」趙高因曰：「夫沙丘之謀，丞相與焉。

translations.literal: ” Zhao Gao thereupon said: “As for the plot at Shaxiu, the chancellor shared in it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhao Gao then said: “The chancellor shared in the plot at Shaxiu.

sentences.zh: 今陛下已立為帝，而丞貴不益，此其意亦望裂地而王矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has been enthroned as emperor, yet the chancellor’s honors have not increased—this shows his intent is also to hope to carve out territory and become a king.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is already emperor, yet the chancellor’s honors have not increased—his intent is surely to carve out territory and make himself a king.

sentences.zh: 且陛下不問臣，臣不敢言。

translations.literal: Moreover, had Your Majesty not asked me, I would not have dared to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Had Your Majesty not asked me, I would not have dared to speak.

sentences.zh: 丞相長男李由為三川守，楚盜陳勝等皆丞相傍縣之子，以故楚盜公行，過三川城，守不肯擊。

translations.literal: The chancellor’s eldest son Li You is governor of Sanchuan; the Chu bandits Chen Sheng and the rest are all sons of districts neighboring the chancellor’s—therefore the Chu bandits travel openly; passing the cities of Sanchuan, the governor would not strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor’s eldest son Li You is governor of Sanchuan; the Chu rebels Chen Sheng and the rest are all from districts neighboring the chancellor’s fief—therefore the Chu rebels travel openly, and when they pass Sanchuan’s cities the governor will not attack.

sentences.zh: 高聞其文書相往來，未得其審，故未敢以聞。

translations.literal: I have heard that their documents go back and forth to one another; I have not obtained proof, and therefore did not dare report it.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard their correspondence goes back and forth; I have not obtained proof, and therefore did not dare report it.

sentences.zh: 且丞相居外，權重於陛下。

translations.literal: Moreover the chancellor dwells outside and his authority outweighs Your Majesty’s.”
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the chancellor acts outside the palace, and his authority outweighs Your Majesty’s.”

sentences.zh: 」二世以為然，欲案丞相，恐其不審，乃先使人按驗三川守與盜通狀。

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor thought this correct, wished to proceed against the chancellor, but feared the matter was not verified; he thereupon first sent men to investigate and verify the San River governor’s collusion with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor agreed, wished to move against the chancellor, but feared the evidence was not firm; he first sent men to investigate whether the San River governor had colluded with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 李斯聞之，因上書言趙高之短曰：「高擅利擅害，與陛下無異。

translations.literal: Li Si, hearing of this, thereupon submitted a memorial stating Zhao Gao’s faults, saying: “Gao monopolizes benefit and harm alike and is no different from Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Si heard of this, he memorialized the throne on Zhao Gao’s faults: “Gao wields profit and punishment at will and is no different from Your Majesty.”

sentences.zh: 昔田常相齊簡公，竊其恩威，下得百姓，上得群臣，卒弒齊簡公而取齊國，此天下所明知也。

translations.literal: Formerly Tian Chang served as chancellor to Duke Jian of Qi, stole his favor and awesomeness, won the common people below and the ministers above, and in the end assassinated Duke Jian of Qi and seized the state of Qi—this is what all under Heaven clearly knows.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Tian Chang was chancellor to Duke Jian of Qi, stole his favor and authority, won the people below and the ministers above, and finally assassinated Duke Jian and seized Qi—this all the world knows.”

sentences.zh: 今高有邪佚之志，危反之行，私家之富，若田氏之於齊矣，而又貪慾無厭，求利不止，列勢次主，其欲無窮，劫陛下之威信，其志若韓□為韓安相也。

translations.literal: Now Gao has perverse and dissolute intent, conduct that endangers and overturns, and private family wealth like the Tian clan toward Qi; moreover he is insatiably greedy, seeking profit without cease. His arrayed power ranks second to the ruler; his desires are boundless. He seizes Your Majesty’s prestige and authority—his intent is like Han□ serving as chancellor of Han for Lord An.
translations.idiomatic: Now Gao harbors perverse designs and conduct that threatens rebellion; his private wealth rivals the Tian clan’s hold on Qi. He is insatiably greedy, his power ranks just below the throne, his desires know no limit, and he usurps Your Majesty’s prestige and authority—his intent is like Han□ as chancellor to Lord An of Han.”

sentences.zh: 陛下不圖，臣恐其必為變也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not take thought, your servant fears he will surely bring about revolt.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not act, I fear he will surely rebel.”

sentences.zh: 」二世曰：「何哉！

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor said: “What is this!
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor said: “What nonsense!”

sentences.zh: 夫高，故宦人也，然不為安肆志，不以危易心，潔行修善，自使至此，以忠得進，以信守位，朕實賢之。

translations.literal: Gao is a former palace eunuch, yet he does not indulge his will in ease, does not change his heart because of peril, purifies his conduct and cultivates goodness, and by himself has reached this point—advancing through loyalty, holding his post through faithfulness. I truly esteem him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao is a former palace eunuch, yet he does not indulge himself in comfort or change his heart in danger; he has cultivated his conduct and risen to this post through loyalty and trustworthiness. I truly esteem him.”

sentences.zh: 而君疑之，何也？

translations.literal: Yet you, sir, suspect him—why?
translations.idiomatic: Why do you suspect him?”

sentences.zh: 且朕非屬趙君，當誰任哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, if I do not entrust matters to Lord Zhao, whom should I employ!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, if I do not entrust affairs to Lord Zhao, whom should I employ?”

sentences.zh: 且趙君為人，精廉強力，下知人情，上能適朕，君其勿疑！

translations.literal: Moreover, in his person Lord Zhao is refined, incorruptible, and forceful; below he understands human feelings, above he can suit me—do not doubt him!
translations.idiomatic: Lord Zhao is refined, incorruptible, and forceful; he understands men below and suits me above—you must not doubt him!”

sentences.zh: 」二世雅愛信高，恐李斯殺之，乃私告趙高。

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor had long loved and trusted Gao; fearing Li Si would kill him, he privately informed Zhao Gao.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor had long favored and trusted Gao; fearing Li Si would kill him, he told Zhao Gao in private.

sentences.zh: 高曰：「丞相所患者獨高，高已死，丞相即欲為田常所為。

translations.literal: Gao said: “The only one the chancellor worries about is Gao. Once Gao is dead, the chancellor will at once do what Tian Chang did.
translations.idiomatic: Gao said: “The chancellor’s only worry is me. Once I am dead, he will do what Tian Chang did.”

sentences.zh: 是時，盜賊益多，而關中捽髮東擊盜者無已。

translations.literal: At this time bandits grew ever more numerous, while within the passes men were conscripted by the hair to strike bandits eastward without cease.
translations.idiomatic: At this time rebels grew ever more numerous, while within the passes men were pressed into service and sent east to fight rebels without cease.

sentences.zh: 右丞相馮去疾、左丞相李斯、將軍馮劫進諫曰：「關東群盜並起，秦發兵追擊，所殺亡甚眾，然猶不止。

translations.literal: The right chancellor Feng Quji, the left chancellor Li Si, and the general Feng Jie advanced remonstrance, saying: “Bandits east of the passes have risen together; Qin sends troops in pursuit and the killed and dead are very many, yet they still do not stop.
translations.idiomatic: The right chancellor Feng Quji, the left chancellor Li Si, and General Feng Jie remonstrated: “Rebels east of the passes have risen everywhere; Qin sends troops in pursuit and kills vast numbers, yet they still do not stop.”

sentences.zh: 盜多，皆以戍、漕、轉、作事苦，稅賦大也。

translations.literal: Bandits are many—all because frontier service, canal transport, relay transport, and corvée labor are bitter, and taxes and levies are heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels multiply because frontier service, canal transport, relay transport, and corvée labor are crushing, and taxes are heavy.”

sentences.zh: 請且止阿房宮作者，減省四邊戍、轉。

translations.literal: We beg to halt for the time being work on Epang Palace and reduce frontier garrisons and relay transport on the four sides.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that work on Epang Palace be halted for now and that frontier garrisons and transport on all sides be reduced.”

sentences.zh: 」二世曰：「凡所為貴有天下者，得肆意極欲，主重明法，下不敢為非，以制御海內矣。

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor said: “Whoever is honored with possessing All under Heaven may indulge his will to the utmost. The ruler is weighty and clarifies the laws; those below dare not do wrong—thus he controls the realm within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor said: “Whoever is honored with possessing the realm may indulge his will to the utmost. The ruler is august and makes the laws clear; those below dare not do wrong—thus he controls the empire.”

sentences.zh: 夫虞、夏之主，貴為天子，親處窮苦之實以徇百姓，尚何於法！

translations.literal: The lords of Yu and Xia, honored as Sons of Heaven, personally endured the reality of poverty and hardship to yield to the common people—what need had they of law!
translations.idiomatic: The rulers of Yu and Xia, though honored as Sons of Heaven, personally endured poverty to yield to the people—what need had they of law!”

sentences.zh: 且先帝起諸侯，兼天下，天下已定，外攘四夷以安邊境，作宮室以章得意，而君觀先帝功業有緒。

translations.literal: Moreover, the late emperor rose from among the feudal lords, united All under Heaven; once the realm was settled, he drove off the four barbarians abroad to secure the borders and built palaces to display his satisfaction—and you, sirs, see the late emperor’s achievements taking shape.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the late emperor rose from the feudal lords and united the realm; once it was settled, he drove back the four barbarians to secure the borders and built palaces to display his triumph—and you see his achievements taking shape.”

sentences.zh: 今朕即位，二年之間，群盜並起，君不能禁，又欲罷先帝之所為，是上無以報先帝，次不為朕盡忠力，何以在位！

translations.literal: Now I have taken the throne; within two years bandits have risen together and you cannot forbid them, yet you also wish to abandon what the late emperor did—above, there is no way to answer the late emperor; next, you do not exhaust loyalty and strength for me—how can you hold office!
translations.idiomatic: I have reigned barely two years, yet rebels rise everywhere and you cannot stop them—and now you wish to abandon the late emperor’s works! Above, you fail the late emperor; below, you fail me—how can you hold office!”

sentences.zh: 」下去疾、斯、劫吏，案責他罪。

translations.literal: ” He sent Quji, Si, and Jie down to the law officers and had them prosecuted and charged with other crimes.
translations.idiomatic: ” He handed Quji, Si, and Jie over to the law officers and had them prosecuted on other charges.

sentences.zh: 去疾、劫自殺，獨李斯就獄。

translations.literal: Quji and Jie killed themselves; only Li Si entered prison.
translations.idiomatic: Quji and Jie killed themselves; only Li Si was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 二世以屬趙高治之，責斯與子由謀反狀，皆收捕宗族、賓客。

translations.literal: The Second Emperor entrusted him to Zhao Gao to try the case, charged Si and his son You with plotting rebellion, and had all their clans and retainers arrested.
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor entrusted the case to Zhao Gao, charged Li Si and his son You with rebellion, and had their entire clans and retainers arrested.

sentences.zh: 趙高治斯，榜掠千餘，不勝痛，自誣服。

translations.literal: Zhao Gao tried Si, flogged him more than a thousand times; unable to bear the pain, he falsely confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao tried Li Si and flogged him more than a thousand times; unable to bear the pain, he falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 斯所以不死者，自負其辯，有功，實無反心，欲上書自陳，幸二世寤而赦之。

translations.literal: The reason Si did not die was that he relied on his eloquence, his achievements, and that he truly had no heart of rebellion; he wished to submit a memorial to state his case himself, hoping the Second Emperor would awaken and pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si did not die because he trusted in his eloquence and his achievements and knew he had no heart of rebellion; he hoped to submit a memorial and win the Second Emperor’s pardon.

sentences.zh: 乃從獄中上書曰：「臣為丞相治民，三十餘年矣。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial from prison, saying: “Your servant has served as chancellor governing the people for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized from prison: “Your servant has served as chancellor governing the people for more than thirty years.”

sentences.zh: 逮秦地之狹隘，不過千里，兵數十萬。

translations.literal: When Qin’s territory was narrow and confined, it did not exceed a thousand li, and troops numbered several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin’s territory was narrow and confined, it did not exceed a thousand li, and its troops numbered only several hundred thousand.”

sentences.zh: 臣盡薄材，陰行謀臣，資之金玉，使遊說諸侯；

translations.literal: Your servant exhausted his slight talents, secretly sent plotting ministers, supplied them with gold and jade, and had them go persuading the feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: I exhausted my slight talents, secretly sent plotting ministers, supplied them with gold and jade, and had them go to persuade the feudal lords;

sentences.zh: 陰修甲兵，飭政教，官鬥士，尊功臣；

translations.literal: secretly repaired armor and weapons, rectified government and teaching, assigned offices to fighting men, and honored meritorious ministers;
translations.idiomatic: secretly repaired armor and weapons, rectified government and teaching, assigned offices to fighting men, and honored meritorious ministers;

sentences.zh: 故終以脅韓，弱魏，破燕、趙，夷齊、楚，卒兼六國，虜其王，立秦為天子。

translations.literal: therefore in the end by coercion took Han, weakened Wei, broke Yan and Zhao, extinguished Qi and Chu, finally united the Six States, captured their kings, and established Qin as Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: and so in the end coerced Han, weakened Wei, broke Yan and Zhao, extinguished Qi and Chu, united the Six States, captured their kings, and established Qin as Son of Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 又北逐胡、貉，南定北越，以見秦之強。

translations.literal: Again he drove off the Hu and Mo in the north and settled Northern Yue in the south, showing Qin’s strength.
translations.idiomatic: I also drove off the Hu and Mo in the north and settled Northern Yue in the south, showing Qin’s strength.”

sentences.zh: 更克畫，平斗斛、度量，文章布之天下，以樹秦之名。

translations.literal: He further overcame and planned, standardized bushels and dou, weights and measures, and spread written ordinances throughout All under Heaven to plant Qin’s name.
translations.idiomatic: I further devised reforms, standardized bushels, weights, and measures, and spread written ordinances throughout the realm to establish Qin’s name.”

sentences.zh: 此皆臣之罪也，臣當死久矣！

translations.literal: All these are your servant’s crimes; your servant ought to have died long ago!
translations.idiomatic: All these are my crimes; I ought to have died long ago!”

sentences.zh: 上幸盡其能力，乃得至今。

translations.literal: Your Majesty was fortunate to exhaust his abilities, and only then did he reach the present.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty was gracious enough to use me to the full, and only thus have I survived until now.”

sentences.zh: 願陛下察之！

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to examine this!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider this!”

sentences.zh: 」書上，趙高使吏棄去不奏，曰：「囚安得上書！

translations.literal: ” When the letter was submitted, Zhao Gao had the clerk discard it and not present it, saying: “How may a prisoner submit a memorial!
translations.idiomatic: ” When the memorial was submitted, Zhao Gao had the clerk discard it and not present it, saying: “How may a prisoner submit a memorial!”

sentences.zh: 趙高使其客十餘輩詐為御史、謁者、侍中，更往覆訊斯，斯更以其實對，輒使人復榜之。

translations.literal: Zhao Gao had more than ten of his retainers falsely pose as imperial censors, petitioners, and palace attendants, go repeatedly to re-examine Si; Si again answered with the truth, and he would at once have men flog him again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao had more than ten retainers pose as censors, petitioners, and palace attendants and repeatedly re-examine Li Si; each time Si answered truthfully, they had him flogged again.

sentences.zh: 後二世使人驗斯，斯以為如前，終不更言。

translations.literal: Later the Second Emperor sent men to verify Si’s case; Si thought it was as before and in the end did not change his words.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Second Emperor sent men to verify the case, Li Si thought it was the same as before and would not change his testimony.

sentences.zh: 辭服，奏當上。

translations.literal: He confessed guilt; the report of the proper sentence was submitted upward.
translations.idiomatic: He confessed; the sentence was reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 二世喜曰：「微趙君，幾為丞相所賣！

translations.literal: The Second Emperor was pleased and said: “But for Lord Zhao, I would nearly have been sold out by the chancellor!
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor was pleased and said: “But for Lord Zhao, I would nearly have been betrayed by the chancellor!”

sentences.zh: 」及二世所使案三川守由者至，則楚兵已擊殺之。

translations.literal: ” When those the Second Emperor had sent to investigate San River governor You arrived, Chu troops had already attacked and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: ” When the men the Second Emperor had sent to investigate San River governor You arrived, Chu troops had already attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 使者來，會職責相下吏，高皆妄為反辭以相傅會，遂具斯五刑，論腰斬咸陽市。

translations.literal: When the envoys came, it happened that duties were being assigned to subordinate law officers; Gao all falsely made words of rebellion to link and fit together, and thereupon completed on Si the five punishments, sentencing him to waist-slicing in the marketplace of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys arrived, the case was being handed to subordinate officers; Gao fabricated charges of rebellion to fit the case, imposed the full five punishments on Li Si, and sentenced him to be cut in two at the waist in the Xianyang marketplace.

sentences.zh: 斯出獄，與其中子俱執。

translations.literal: Si came out of prison and was seized together with his second son.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si came out of prison and was seized together with his second son.

sentences.zh: 顧謂其中子曰：「吾欲與若復牽黃犬，俱出上蔡東門逐狡兔，豈可得乎！

translations.literal: He looked back and said to his second son: “I wish to go with you again leading a yellow dog, both of us out the eastern gate of Shangcai chasing crafty hares—how could that be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: He turned to his second son and said: “I wish I could go with you again, leading a yellow dog out the eastern gate of Shangcai to chase hares—how could that be now!”

sentences.zh: 」遂父子相哭，而夷三族。

translations.literal: ” Father and son thereupon wept together, and the three clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: ” Father and son wept together, and all three clans were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 二世乃以趙高為丞相，事無大小皆決焉。

translations.literal: The Second Emperor thereupon made Zhao Gao chancellor; matters great and small were all decided by him.
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor then made Zhao Gao chancellor; great and small affairs were all decided by him.

sentences.zh: 17項梁已破章邯於東阿，引兵西，北至定陶，再破秦軍。

translations.literal: 17. Xiang Liang had already defeated Zhang Han at Dong’e, led his army west, reached north to Dingtao, and again defeated Qin troops.
translations.idiomatic: 17. Xiang Liang had already defeated Zhang Han at Dong’e, marched west to Dingtao, and again defeated Qin forces.

sentences.zh: 項羽、沛公又與秦軍戰於雍丘，大破之，斬李由。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu and the Lord of Pei again fought Qin troops at Yongqiu, routed them greatly, and beheaded Li You.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu and the Lord of Pei again fought Qin at Yongqiu, routed them, and beheaded Li You.

sentences.zh: 項梁益輕秦，有驕色。

translations.literal: Xiang Liang grew ever more contemptuous of Qin and showed arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Liang grew increasingly contemptuous of Qin and showed arrogance.

sentences.zh: 宋義諫曰：「戰勝而將驕卒惰者，敗。

translations.literal: Song Yi remonstrated, saying: “When victory is won yet the general grows arrogant and the soldiers grow slack—defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yi remonstrated: “When the general grows arrogant and the soldiers slack after victory—defeat follows.”

sentences.zh: 今卒少惰矣，秦兵日益，臣為君畏之。

translations.literal: Now the soldiers are somewhat slack; Qin troops grow daily—I fear this for you, my lord.
translations.idiomatic: Your soldiers are already growing slack while Qin’s forces grow daily—I fear this for you, my lord.”

sentences.zh: 」項梁弗聽。

translations.literal: ” Xiang Liang did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xiang Liang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 餘乃使宋義使於齊，道遇齊使者高陵君顯，曰：「公將見武信君乎？

translations.literal: Yu thereupon sent Song Yi on a mission to Qi; on the road he met the Qi envoy Lord Xian of Gaoling and said: “Will you, sir, be going to see Lord Xinwu?
translations.idiomatic: Yu then sent Song Yi on a mission to Qi; on the road he met the Qi envoy Lord Xian of Gaoling and said: “Are you going to see Lord Xinwu?”

translations.literal: ” He said: “Yes.
translations.idiomatic: ” He said: “Yes.”

sentences.zh: 」曰：「臣論武信君軍必敗。

translations.literal: ” Song Yi said: “I maintain that Lord Xinwu’s army will surely be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: ” Song Yi said: “I predict Lord Xinwu’s army will surely be defeated.”

sentences.zh: 公徐行即免死，疾行則及禍。

translations.literal: If you, sir, go slowly you will escape death; if you go swiftly you will meet disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Go slowly and you will escape death; go swiftly and you will meet disaster.”

sentences.zh: 」二世悉起兵益章邯擊楚軍，大破之定陶，項梁死。

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor mustered all troops to reinforce Zhang Han in attacking the Chu army, routed them greatly at Dingtao, and Xiang Liang died.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor mustered all troops to reinforce Zhang Han; he routed the Chu army at Dingtao and Xiang Liang was killed.

sentences.zh: 時連雨，自七月至九月。

translations.literal: At this time rain fell continuously from the seventh month to the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell continuously from the seventh month through the ninth.

sentences.zh: 項羽、沛公攻外黃未下，去，攻陳留。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu and the Lord of Pei attacked Waihuang but did not take it; they left and attacked Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu and the Lord of Pei attacked Waihuang without success, withdrew, and attacked Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 聞武信君死，士卒恐，乃與將軍呂臣引兵而東，徙懷王自盱眙都彭城。

translations.literal: Hearing that Lord Xinwu had died, the soldiers were afraid; they thereupon with the general Lü Chen led troops eastward and moved King Huai from Xuyi to make Pengcheng his capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Lord Xinwu was dead, the troops were afraid; they marched east with General Lü Chen and moved King Huai from Xuyi to Pengcheng as his capital.

sentences.zh: 呂臣軍彭城東，項羽軍彭城西，沛公軍碭。
