translations.literal: Lü Chen encamped east of Pengcheng; Xiang Yu encamped west of Pengcheng; the Lord of Pei encamped at Dang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chen encamped east of Pengcheng, Xiang Yu west of Pengcheng, and the Lord of Pei at Dang.

sentences.zh: 魏豹下魏二十餘城，楚懷王立豹為魏王。

translations.literal: Wei Bao took more than twenty cities of Wei; King Huai of Chu installed Bao as king of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bao took more than twenty cities of Wei, and King Huai of Chu made him king of Wei.

sentences.zh: 後九月，楚懷王並呂臣、項羽軍，自將之；

translations.literal: In the intercalary ninth month, King Huai of Chu combined the armies of Lü Chen and Xiang Yu and personally commanded them;
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary ninth month, King Huai of Chu combined the armies of Lü Chen and Xiang Yu and took command himself;

sentences.zh: 以沛公為碭郡長，封武安侯，將碭郡兵；

translations.literal: he made the Lord of Pei magistrate of Dang commandery, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wu’an, and had him command Dang commandery troops;
translations.idiomatic: he made the Lord of Pei magistrate of Dang commandery, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wu’an, and put him in command of Dang troops;

sentences.zh: 封項羽為長安侯，號為魯公；

translations.literal: he enfeoffed Xiang Yu as Marquis of Chang’an, styled Lord of Lu;
translations.idiomatic: he enfeoffed Xiang Yu as Marquis of Chang’an with the title Lord of Lu;

sentences.zh: 呂臣為司徒，其父呂青為令尹。

translations.literal: he made Lü Chen Minister of the Masses, and his father Lü Qing Grand Minister.
translations.idiomatic: he made Lü Chen Minister of the Masses and his father Lü Qing Grand Minister.

sentences.zh: 18章邯已破項梁，以為楚地兵不足憂，乃渡河，北擊趙，大破之。

translations.literal: 18. Zhang Han, having defeated Xiang Liang, thought Chu’s forces were not worth worrying over; he thereupon crossed the river, attacked Zhao in the north, and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: 18. Zhang Han, having defeated Xiang Liang, thought Chu’s forces were no longer a concern; he crossed the river north, attacked Zhao, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 引兵至邯鄲，皆徙其民河內，夷其城郭。

translations.literal: He led troops to Handan, relocated all its people to Henei, and leveled its walls and suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to Handan, relocated all its people to Henei, and leveled its walls.

sentences.zh: 張耳與趙王歇走入巨鹿城，王離圍之。

translations.literal: Zhang Er and King Xie of Zhao fled into the city of Julu; Wang Li besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er and King Xie of Zhao fled into Julu; Wang Li besieged them.

sentences.zh: 陳餘北收常山兵，得數萬人，軍巨鹿北。

translations.literal: Chen Yu gathered Changshan troops in the north, obtained several tens of thousands of men, and encamped north of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu gathered Changshan troops in the north, raised several tens of thousands of men, and encamped north of Julu.

sentences.zh: 章邯軍巨鹿南棘原。

translations.literal: Zhang Han’s army was south of Julu at Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han’s army lay south of Julu at Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 趙數請救於楚。

translations.literal: Zhao repeatedly asked Chu for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao repeatedly asked Chu for aid.

sentences.zh: 高陵君顯在楚，見楚王曰：「宋義論武信君之軍必敗，居數日，軍果敗。

translations.literal: Lord Xian of Gaoling was in Chu; he saw the King of Chu and said: “Song Yi maintained that Lord Xinwu’s army would surely be defeated; within several days the army was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Xian of Gaoling was in Chu; he saw the King of Chu and said: “Song Yi predicted that Lord Xinwu’s army would be defeated, and within days it was.”

sentences.zh: 兵未戰而先見敗征，此可謂知兵矣。

translations.literal: Before the troops had fought he already saw the signs of defeat—this may be called understanding warfare.
translations.idiomatic: He foresaw defeat before battle was joined—this may be called understanding warfare.”

sentences.zh: 」王召宋義與計事而大說之，因置以為上將軍。

translations.literal: ” The king summoned Song Yi to plan affairs and was greatly pleased with him; he thereupon installed him as supreme general.
translations.idiomatic: ” The king summoned Song Yi to discuss strategy, was greatly pleased, and made him supreme general.

sentences.zh: 項羽為次將，范增為末將，以救趙。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu was second general, Fan Zeng last general, to rescue Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu was made second general and Fan Zeng last general, to rescue Zhao.

sentences.zh: 諸別將皆屬宋義，號為「卿子冠軍」。

translations.literal: All the separate generals were subordinated to Song Yi, styled “Lordling Champion.”
translations.idiomatic: All subordinate generals were placed under Song Yi, who was styled “Lordling Champion.”

sentences.zh: 初，楚懷王與諸將約：「先入定關中者王之。

translations.literal: Earlier, King Huai of Chu had made a covenant with the generals: “Whoever first settles and enters Guanzhong shall be king.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, King Huai of Chu had agreed with his generals: “Whoever first enters and settles Guanzhong shall be king.”

sentences.zh: 」當是時，秦兵強，常乘勝逐北，諸將莫利先入關。

translations.literal: ” At this time Qin troops were strong and constantly pursued the defeated northward; none of the generals thought it profitable to enter Guanzhong first.
translations.idiomatic: ” At that time Qin was strong and always pursued defeated foes; none of the generals thought it profitable to enter Guanzhong first.

sentences.zh: 獨項羽怨秦之殺項梁，奮勢願與沛公西入關。

translations.literal: Only Xiang Yu resented Qin for killing Xiang Liang; rousing his strength, he wished to enter Guanzhong west together with the Lord of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xiang Yu, resenting Qin for killing Xiang Liang, was eager to march west into Guanzhong with the Lord of Pei.

sentences.zh: 懷王諸老將皆曰：「項羽為人，慓悍猾賊，嘗攻襄城，襄城無遺類，皆坑之，諸所過無不殘滅。

translations.literal: King Huai’s veteran generals all said: “In his person Xiang Yu is fierce, violent, and crafty as a thief. He once attacked Xiangcheng; Xiangcheng had no survivors left—all were buried alive. Everywhere he passes there is nothing not destroyed and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: King Huai’s veteran generals all said: “Xiang Yu is fierce, violent, and treacherous. He once attacked Xiangcheng and buried every survivor alive; everywhere he passes he leaves nothing but ruin.”

sentences.zh: 且楚數進取，前陳王、項梁皆敗，不如更遣長者，扶義而西，告諭秦父兄。

translations.literal: Moreover Chu has repeatedly advanced to attack; the former King Chen and Xiang Liang were both defeated. It is better to send another elder, supporting righteousness westward to announce and instruct the elders and elder brothers of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Chu has repeatedly attacked and failed; King Chen and Xiang Liang both met defeat. It is better to send a worthy elder west in the name of righteousness to win over the elders of Qin.”

sentences.zh: 秦父兄苦其主久矣，今誠得長者往，無侵暴，宜可下。

translations.literal: The elders and elder brothers of Qin have long suffered under their ruler; if today a true elder is sent who does not invade or brutalize, they should be reducible.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qin have long suffered under their ruler; if a worthy elder goes who does not brutalize them, the region should submit.”

sentences.zh: 項羽不可遣，獨沛公素寬大長者，可遣。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu may not be sent; only the Lord of Pei has always been magnanimous and an elder—he may be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu must not be sent; only the Lord of Pei, who has always been magnanimous and worthy, should go.”

sentences.zh: 」懷王乃不許項羽，而遣沛公西略地，收陳王、項梁散卒以伐秦。

translations.literal: ” King Huai thereupon did not permit Xiang Yu but sent the Lord of Pei west to seize territory, gathering the scattered troops of King Chen and Xiang Liang to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: ” King Huai therefore refused Xiang Yu and sent the Lord of Pei west to seize territory, gathering the scattered troops of King Chen and Xiang Liang to attack Qin.

sentences.zh: 沛公道碭，至陽城與槓里，攻秦壁，破其二軍。

translations.literal: The Lord of Pei went by way of Dang, reached Yangcheng and Gangli, attacked Qin fortified camps, and broke two of their armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Pei marched by way of Dang to Yangcheng and Gangli, attacked Qin fortified camps, and broke two of their armies.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，齊將田都畔田榮，助楚救趙。

translations.literal: 1. Winter, tenth month—the Qi general Tian Du turned against Tian Rong and aided Chu in rescuing Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the tenth month, the Qi general Tian Du broke with Tian Rong and aided Chu in rescuing Zhao.

sentences.zh: 2沛公攻破東郡尉於成武。

translations.literal: 2. The Lord of Pei defeated the commandant of Dong commandery at Chengwu.
translations.idiomatic: 2. The Lord of Pei defeated the commandant of Dong commandery at Chengwu.

sentences.zh: 3宋義行至安陽，留四十六日不進。

translations.literal: 3. Song Yi marched to Anyang and halted forty-six days without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: 3. Song Yi reached Anyang and halted forty-six days without advancing.

sentences.zh: 項羽曰：「秦圍趙急，宜疾引兵渡河；

translations.literal: Xiang Yu said: “Qin besieges Zhao urgently; we ought swiftly to lead troops across the river;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu said: “Qin is pressing the siege of Zhao; we ought to cross the river at once;

sentences.zh: 楚擊其外，趙應其內，破秦軍必矣。

translations.literal: Chu strikes them from without, Zhao responds from within—breaking Qin’s army is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Chu strikes from without and Zhao responds from within—the Qin army is sure to be broken.”

sentences.zh: 」宋義曰：「不然。

translations.literal: ” Song Yi said: “Not so.
translations.idiomatic: ” Song Yi said: “Not so.”

sentences.zh: 夫搏牛之虻，不可以破蟣虱。

translations.literal: The gadfly that strikes an ox cannot be used to crush lice.
translations.idiomatic: The gadfly that strikes an ox cannot be used to crush lice.”

sentences.zh: 今秦攻趙，戰勝則兵疲，我承其敝；

translations.literal: Now if Qin attacks Zhao and wins, its troops will be weary and we can take advantage of their exhaustion;
translations.idiomatic: If Qin attacks Zhao and wins, its troops will be weary and we can take advantage of their exhaustion;

sentences.zh: 不勝，則我引兵鼓行而西，必舉秦矣。

translations.literal: if it does not win, then we lead troops beating drums in march westward and will surely take Qin.
translations.idiomatic: if it does not win, we march west with drums beating and will surely take Qin.”

sentences.zh: 故不如先斗秦、趙。

translations.literal: Therefore it is better first to let Qin and Zhao fight.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is better to let Qin and Zhao fight first.”

sentences.zh: 夫被堅執銳，義不如公；

translations.literal: In wearing armor and wielding sharp weapons, Yi is not equal to you, sir;
translations.idiomatic: In wearing armor and wielding sharp weapons, I am not your equal;

sentences.zh: 坐運籌策，公不如義。

translations.literal: in sitting and plotting strategies, you, sir, are not equal to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: but in sitting and plotting strategy, you are not my equal.”

sentences.zh: 」因下令軍中曰：「有猛如虎，狠如羊，貪如狼，強不可使者，皆斬之！

translations.literal: ” He thereupon issued orders in the army, saying: “Whoever is fierce as a tiger, ruthless as a sheep, greedy as a wolf, or so strong he cannot be employed—all are to be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: ” He then ordered the army: “Any man fierce as a tiger, ruthless as a sheep, greedy as a wolf, or so overbearing he cannot be commanded—all shall be beheaded!”

sentences.zh: 」乃遣其子宋襄相齊，身送之至無鹽，飲酒高會。

translations.literal: ” He then sent his son Song Xiang as chancellor to Qi, personally escorting him as far as Wuyan, where they drank wine at a grand gathering.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then sent his son Song Xiang as envoy to Qi, personally escorted him to Wuyan, and held a grand feast with wine.”

sentences.zh: 天寒，大雨，士卒凍饑。

translations.literal: The weather was cold, rain heavy; soldiers froze and starved.
translations.idiomatic: The weather turned cold and rain poured down; the troops froze and went hungry.

sentences.zh: 項羽曰：「將戮力而攻秦，久留不行。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu said, “The generals are to join forces and attack Qin, yet we have long stayed and not advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu said, “We were to unite and strike Qin, yet we have lingered here without advancing.

sentences.zh: 今歲饑民貧，士卒食半菽，軍無見糧，乃飲酒高會；

translations.literal: This year there is famine and the people are poor; soldiers eat half beans, the army has no grain in sight, yet you hold grand drinking feasts;
translations.idiomatic: This year the people are starving and poor; the men eat half rations of beans, the army has no grain in sight, yet you hold grand banquets;

sentences.zh: 不引兵渡河，因趙食，與趙並力攻秦，乃曰『承其敝』。

translations.literal: you do not lead the army across the river to rely on Zhao for food and join Zhao in attacking Qin, yet speak of ‘reaping their exhaustion.’
translations.idiomatic: you will not cross the river to draw on Zhao's supplies and join Zhao in attacking Qin, yet talk of ‘waiting until they are worn out.’

sentences.zh: 夫以秦之強，攻新造之趙，其勢必舉。

translations.literal: With Qin's strength attacking a newly made Zhao, the trend is sure to be that Zhao is taken.
translations.idiomatic: With Qin's might against a newly founded Zhao, Zhao is sure to fall.

sentences.zh: 趙舉秦強，何敝之承！

translations.literal: If Zhao is taken, Qin grows strong—what exhaustion is there to reap!
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhao falls, Qin only grows stronger—what ‘exhaustion’ is there to reap!

sentences.zh: 且國兵新破，王坐不安席，掃境內而專屬於將軍，國家安危，在此一舉。

translations.literal: Moreover the state's army has just been defeated; the king sits as on pins and needles, has swept the realm and entrusted everything to the general—the state's safety or peril hangs on this one move.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover our army has just been beaten; the king cannot sit at ease, has swept the realm and entrusted everything to you—the fate of the state hangs on this one move.

sentences.zh: 今不恤士卒而徇其私，非社稷之臣也！

translations.literal: Now you do not pity the soldiers yet indulge your private ends—you are no minister of the altars of soil and grain!
translations.idiomatic: You show no care for the troops yet indulge yourself—you are no true servant of the state!

sentences.zh: 十一月，項羽晨朝將軍宋義，即其帳中斬宋義頭。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Xiang Yu at dawn attended upon General Song Yi and in his tent beheaded Song Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Xiang Yu attended General Song Yi at dawn and beheaded him in his tent.

sentences.zh: 出令軍中曰：「宋義與齊謀反楚，楚王陰令籍誅之！

translations.literal: He issued an order in the army, saying, “Song Yi plotted rebellion with Qi; King Huai secretly ordered Ji to execute him!
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed to the army, “Song Yi conspired with Qi against Chu; King Huai secretly ordered Ji to kill him!

sentences.zh: 」當是時，諸將皆懾服，莫敢枝梧，皆曰：「首立楚者，將軍家也，今將軍誅亂。

translations.literal: ” At that time the various generals were all awed into submission; none dared resist, and all said, “It was the general's house that first raised Chu; now the general has punished rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: ” At that time every general submitted in awe; none dared resist, and all said, “Your house first raised Chu; now you have put down treason.

sentences.zh: 」乃相與共立羽為假上將軍。

translations.literal: ” They then together established Yu as acting supreme general.
translations.idiomatic: ” They then jointly made Yu acting supreme general.

sentences.zh: 使人追宋義子，及之齊，殺之。

translations.literal: He sent men to pursue Song Yi's son; catching up with him in Qi, they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men after Song Yi's son; overtaking him in Qi, they killed him.

sentences.zh: 使桓楚報命於懷王。

translations.literal: He sent Huan Chu to report the outcome to King Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Huan Chu to report to King Huai.

sentences.zh: 懷王因使羽為上將軍。

translations.literal: King Huai thereupon made Yu supreme general.
translations.idiomatic: King Huai then appointed Yu supreme general.

sentences.zh: 4十二月，沛公引兵至栗，遇剛武侯，奪其軍四千餘人，並之；

translations.literal: 4 In the twelfth month, the Duke of Pei led his army to Li, met Marquis Wu of Gang, seized his army of more than four thousand men, and merged them;
translations.idiomatic: 4 In the twelfth month, the Duke of Pei marched to Li, met Marquis Wu of Gang, took over his force of more than four thousand men, and absorbed them;

sentences.zh: 與魏將皇欣、武滿軍合攻秦軍，破之。

translations.literal: joined with the Wei generals Huang Xin and Wu Man's armies to attack the Qin army together and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: then joined Wei generals Huang Xin and Wu Man to attack the Qin army and routed it.

sentences.zh: 5故齊王建孫安下濟北，從項羽救趙。

translations.literal: 5 An, grandson of the former King Jian of Qi, came down from Jibei and followed Xiang Yu to rescue Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: 5 An, grandson of the former King Jian of Qi, came down from Jibei to follow Xiang Yu in rescuing Zhao.

sentences.zh: 章邯築甬道屬河，餉王離。

translations.literal: Zhang Han built a raised supply road along the river to provision Wang Li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han built a supply road along the river to feed Wang Li.

sentences.zh: 王離兵食多，急攻巨鹿。

translations.literal: Wang Li's army had ample food and pressed the attack on Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Li's troops were well supplied and pressed hard on Julu.

sentences.zh: 巨鹿城中食盡、兵少，張耳數使人召前陳餘。

translations.literal: In Julu city food was exhausted and troops few; Zhang Er repeatedly sent men to summon Chen Yu forward.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Julu food ran out and troops were few; Zhang Er repeatedly sent for Chen Yu to advance.

sentences.zh: 陳餘度兵少，不敵秦，不敢前。

translations.literal: Chen Yu estimated his troops were few, could not match Qin, and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu judged his force too small to face Qin and did not dare move forward.

sentences.zh: 數月，張耳大怒，怨陳餘，使張黶、陳澤往讓陳餘曰：「始吾與公為刎頸交，今王與耳旦暮且死，而公擁兵數萬，不肯相救，安在其相為死！

translations.literal: After several months Zhang Er was greatly angered and resented Chen Yu; he sent Zhang Yan and Chen Ze to reproach Chen Yu, saying, “At first you and I were sworn friends at the neck; now the king and Er face death morning and evening, yet you hold tens of thousands of troops and refuse to rescue us—where is the meaning of dying for each other!
translations.idiomatic: After months Zhang Er flew into a rage at Chen Yu and sent Zhang Yan and Chen Ze to rebuke him: “We were sworn friends; now the king and I face death any day, yet you hold tens of thousands of men and will not save us—what happened to dying for each other!

sentences.zh: 苟必信，胡不赴秦軍俱死，且有十一二相全。

translations.literal: If you truly trust us, why not go meet the Qin army and die together—perhaps one or two in ten might survive.
translations.idiomatic: If you still trust us, why not march against the Qin army and die together—perhaps one or two in ten might survive.

sentences.zh: 」陳餘曰：「吾度前終不能救趙，徒盡亡軍。

translations.literal: ” Chen Yu said, “I estimate that advancing still cannot save Zhao—it would only exhaust and lose the army.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chen Yu said, “I reckon an advance still cannot save Zhao—it would only wipe out the army for nothing.

sentences.zh: 且餘所以不俱死，欲為趙王、張君報秦。

translations.literal: Moreover the reason I do not die together is that I wish to avenge Zhao and Lord Zhang upon Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I do not die with you is that I mean to avenge the King of Zhao and Lord Zhang against Qin.

sentences.zh: 今必俱死，如以肉委餓虎，何益！

translations.literal: If we must die together now, it is like throwing meat to a starving tiger—what good is it!
translations.idiomatic: To die together now is only to throw meat to a starving tiger—what good would it do!

sentences.zh: 」張黶、陳澤要以俱死，乃使黶、澤將五千人先嘗秦軍，至，皆沒。

translations.literal: ” Zhang Yan and Chen Ze demanded to die together; he then sent Yan and Ze to lead five thousand men to first test the Qin army—when they arrived, all were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhang Yan and Chen Ze insisted on dying together; Chen Yu sent them with five thousand men to probe the Qin army—they were wiped out to a man.

sentences.zh: 當是時，齊師、燕師皆來救趙，張敖亦北收代兵，得萬餘人，來，皆壁餘旁，未敢擊秦。

translations.literal: At that time Qi and Yan armies had all come to rescue Zhao; Zhang Ao also went north to gather Dai troops, got more than ten thousand men, came, and all fortified camps beside Yu—none dared strike Qin.
translations.idiomatic: By then Qi and Yan had come to Zhao's aid; Zhang Ao too gathered more than ten thousand men from Dai in the north—all encamped near Chen Yu and none dared attack Qin.

sentences.zh: 項羽已殺卿子冠軍，威震楚國，乃遣當陽君、薄將軍將卒二萬渡河救巨鹿。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu had already killed the Young Lord Champion; his prestige shook the state of Chu. He then sent Lord Dangyang and General Bo to lead twenty thousand men across the river to rescue Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu had killed the Young Lord Champion and awed all Chu; he sent Lord Dangyang and General Bo with twenty thousand men across the river toward Julu.

sentences.zh: 戰少利，絕章邯甬道，王離軍乏食。

translations.literal: The fighting was slightly favorable; they cut Zhang Han's supply road, and Wang Li's army lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: After minor successes they severed Zhang Han's supply line, and Wang Li's army ran short of food.

sentences.zh: 陳餘復請兵。

translations.literal: Chen Yu again asked for more troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu again asked for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 項羽乃悉引兵渡河，皆沈船，破釜、甑，燒廬舍，持三日糧，以示士卒必死，無一還心。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu then led his entire army across the river, scuttled all boats, smashed cooking pots and steamers, burned huts, and carried only three days' rations—to show the soldiers they must die and have not one thought of return.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu then brought his whole army across the river, scuttled the boats, smashed the pots, burned the camps, and allowed only three days' rations—showing the men they must fight to the death with no thought of return.

sentences.zh: 於是至則圍王離，與秦軍遇，九戰，大破之，章邯引兵卻。

translations.literal: Thereupon on arrival he besieged Wang Li; meeting the Qin army, he fought nine battles, routed them greatly, and Zhang Han drew his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he besieged Wang Li; meeting the Qin army he fought nine engagements, crushed them, and Zhang Han withdrew.

sentences.zh: 諸侯兵乃敢進擊秦軍，遂殺蘇角，虜王離；

translations.literal: The allied armies then dared advance and strike the Qin army; they killed Su Jiao and captured Wang Li;
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the allied armies dare press the attack; they killed Su Jiao and captured Wang Li;

sentences.zh: 涉間不降，自燒殺。

translations.literal: She Jian would not surrender and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: She Jian refused to surrender and burned himself alive.

sentences.zh: 當是時，楚兵冠諸侯軍。

translations.literal: At that time the Chu army stood at the head of the allied armies.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Chu army led all the allied forces.

sentences.zh: 救巨鹿者十餘壁，莫敢縱兵。

translations.literal: Those who had come to rescue Julu numbered more than ten fortified camps; none dared loose their troops.
translations.idiomatic: More than a dozen allied camps had come to relieve Julu, yet none dared commit their troops.

sentences.zh: 及楚擊秦，諸侯將皆從壁上觀。

translations.literal: When Chu struck Qin, the allied generals all watched from their ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu attacked Qin, the allied generals only watched from their walls.

sentences.zh: 楚戰士無不一當十，呼聲動天地，諸侯軍無不人人惴恐。

translations.literal: No Chu fighter failed to match ten; their shouts shook heaven and earth, and in every allied army none failed to tremble in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Every Chu soldier fought as ten; their battle cries shook heaven and earth, and every man in the allied armies trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 於是已破秦軍，項羽召見諸侯將。

translations.literal: When the Qin army had been broken, Xiang Yu summoned the allied generals to audience.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating the Qin army, Xiang Yu summoned the allied generals.

sentences.zh: 諸侯將入轅門，無不膝行而前，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: The allied generals entering the camp gate all advanced on their knees; none dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: Entering his camp gate, the allied generals all crawled forward on their knees and none dared look up at him.

sentences.zh: 項羽由是始為諸侯上將軍。

translations.literal: From this Xiang Yu first became supreme general of the allies.
translations.idiomatic: From this Xiang Yu became supreme commander of the allied armies.

sentences.zh: 諸侯皆屬焉。

translations.literal: The allies all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: All the allies placed themselves under his command.

sentences.zh: 於是趙王歇及張耳乃得出巨鹿城謝諸侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon King Xie of Zhao and Zhang Er were able to leave Julu city and thank the allies.
translations.idiomatic: Then King Xie of Zhao and Zhang Er were able to leave Julu and thank the allied armies.

sentences.zh: 張耳與陳餘相見，責讓陳餘以不肯救趙；

translations.literal: Zhang Er met Chen Yu and reproached him for refusing to rescue Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er met Chen Yu and rebuked him for refusing to save Zhao;

sentences.zh: 及問張黶、陳澤所在，疑陳餘殺之，數以問餘。

translations.literal: when he asked where Zhang Yan and Chen Ze were, he suspected Chen Yu had killed them and repeatedly pressed Yu about it.
translations.idiomatic: when he asked where Zhang Yan and Chen Ze were, he suspected Chen Yu had killed them and questioned him again and again.

sentences.zh: 餘怒曰：「不意君之望臣深也！

translations.literal: Yu said angrily, “I did not expect you to expect so much of your servant!
translations.idiomatic: Yu said angrily, “I did not expect you to demand so much of me!

sentences.zh: 豈以臣為重去將印哉？

translations.literal: Do you think your servant clung to the general's seal out of greed?
translations.idiomatic: Do you think I clung to the seal out of greed?

sentences.zh: 」乃脫解印綬，推予張耳，張耳亦愕不受。

translations.literal: ” He then removed the seal cord and pushed it to Zhang Er; Zhang Er too was startled and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then stripped off the seal cord and thrust it at Zhang Er, who in astonishment refused to take it.

sentences.zh: 陳餘起如廁。

translations.literal: Chen Yu rose and went to the privy.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu rose and went to relieve himself.

sentences.zh: 客有說張耳曰：「臣聞『天與不取，反受其咎。

translations.literal: A guest urged Zhang Er, saying, “Your servant has heard, ‘Heaven gives and you do not take—turn and you receive its curse.
translations.idiomatic: A guest urged Zhang Er: “I have heard, ‘What Heaven offers, if you do not take, you will suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 』今陳將軍與君印，君不受，反天不祥，急取之！

translations.literal: ’ Now General Chen gives you the seal and you do not accept—going against Heaven is inauspicious; take it quickly!
translations.idiomatic: ’ General Chen offers you the seal and you refuse—that offends Heaven; take it at once!

sentences.zh: 」張耳乃佩其印，收其麾下。

translations.literal: ” Zhang Er then wore the seal on his belt and gathered Chen Yu's troops under him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhang Er then fastened on the seal and took command of Chen Yu's troops.

sentences.zh: 而陳餘還，亦望張耳不讓，遂趨出，獨與麾下所善數百人之河上澤中漁獵。

translations.literal: When Chen Yu returned, he too saw that Zhang Er would not yield; he hurried out and alone with several hundred followers he favored went to fish and hunt in the marshes by the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yu returned and saw Zhang Er would not yield the seal, he rushed out and withdrew with a few hundred trusted followers to fish and hunt in the riverside marshes.

sentences.zh: 趙王歇還信都。

translations.literal: King Xie of Zhao returned to Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: King Xie of Zhao returned to Xindu.

sentences.zh: 6春，二月，沛公北擊昌邑，遇彭越，彭越以其兵從沛公。

translations.literal: 6 In spring, second month, the Duke of Pei attacked Changyi in the north, met Peng Yue, and Peng Yue led his troops to follow the Duke of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: 6 In spring, the second month, the Duke of Pei marched north against Changyi, met Peng Yue, and Peng Yue joined him with his troops.

sentences.zh: 越，昌邑人，常漁巨野澤中，為群盜。

translations.literal: Yue was a man of Changyi who often fished in the Juze marshes and became a bandit chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was from Changyi and had long fished in the Juze marshes as leader of a band of robbers.

sentences.zh: 陳勝、項梁之起，澤間少年相聚百餘人，往從彭越曰：「請仲為長。

translations.literal: When Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang rose, youths about the marshes gathered more than a hundred men, went to follow Peng Yue, and said, “We beg Zhong to be our leader.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Sheng and Xiang Liang rose, more than a hundred young men from the marshes came to Peng Yue and said, “We ask you, Zhong, to lead us.

sentences.zh: 」越謝曰：「臣不願也。

translations.literal: ” Yue declined, saying, “Your servant is unwilling.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yue declined: “I am unwilling.

sentences.zh: 」少年強請，乃許，與期旦日日出會，後期者斬。

translations.literal: ” The youths pressed him strongly; he then agreed and set a rendezvous at dawn the next day—whoever came late would be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: ” The youths pressed him until he agreed, fixing a meeting at dawn the next day—latecomers would be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 旦日日出，十餘人後，後者至日中。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day more than ten men were late; the last arrived at midday.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day more than ten men were late; the last did not arrive until noon.

sentences.zh: 於是越謝曰：「臣老，諸君強以為長。

translations.literal: Yue then apologized, saying, “Your servant is old; you gentlemen forced me to be leader.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then said, “I am old, and you forced me to be your leader.

sentences.zh: 今期而多後，不可盡誅，誅最後者一人。

translations.literal: Now many were late for the appointment—I cannot execute you all; I will execute only the last arrival.
translations.idiomatic: So many of you were late that I cannot kill you all—I will kill only the last to arrive.

sentences.zh: 」令校長斬之。

translations.literal: ” He ordered the company commander to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He ordered the company commander to behead that man.

sentences.zh: 皆笑曰：「何至於是！

translations.literal: All laughed and said, “How could it come to this!
translations.idiomatic: They all laughed and said, “Surely not to that extent!

sentences.zh: 請後不敢。

translations.literal: We beg you—latecomers will not dare again.
translations.idiomatic: We promise never to be late again.

sentences.zh: 」於是越引一人斬之，設壇祭，令徒屬，徒屬皆大驚，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: ” Yue then pulled one man forward and beheaded him, set up an altar and offered sacrifice, and summoned the conscripts; the conscripts were all greatly alarmed and none dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yue then had one man brought forward and beheaded, set up an altar and made sacrifice, and assembled the men—all were terrified and none dared look up.

sentences.zh: 乃略地，收諸侯散卒，得千餘人，遂助沛公攻昌邑。

translations.literal: He then raided territory, gathered scattered troops of the allies, got more than a thousand men, and went on to help the Duke of Pei attack Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: He then raided the countryside, gathered scattered allied troops to more than a thousand men, and helped the Duke of Pei attack Changyi.

sentences.zh: 昌邑未下，沛公引兵西過高陽。

translations.literal: Changyi was not taken; the Duke of Pei led his army west past Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Changyi did not fall; the Duke of Pei marched west past Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 高陽人酈食其，家貧落魄，為里監門，沛公麾下騎士適食其里中人，食其見，謂曰：「諸侯將過高陽者數十人，吾問其將皆握齪，好苛禮，自用，不能聽大度之言。

translations.literal: Li Yi of Gaoyang, poor and down on his luck, served as ward gatekeeper. A cavalryman under the Duke of Pei happened to be a fellow townsman of Yi; Yi saw him and said, “Dozens of allied generals have passed through Gaoyang—I have asked about their commanders and all are petty, fond of harsh ritual, self-willed, and unable to heed broad counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi of Gaoyang was poor and down on his luck and served as gatekeeper of his ward. A cavalryman under the Duke of Pei happened to be from his town; Li Yi saw him and said, “Dozens of allied commanders have passed through Gaoyang—I have asked about them all, and they are petty, fussy about ritual, self-willed, and deaf to large-minded counsel.

sentences.zh: 吾聞沛公慢而易人，多大略，此真吾所願從游，莫為我先。

translations.literal: I hear the Duke of Pei is easygoing and treats men lightly, with great strategic vision—he is truly the one I wish to follow; do not let anyone get ahead of me.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the Duke of Pei is easygoing, approachable, and full of grand design—he is truly the man I wish to serve; do not let anyone reach him before me.

sentences.zh: 若見沛公，謂曰：『臣里中有酈生，六十餘，長八尺，人皆謂之狂生。

translations.literal: If you see the Duke of Pei, tell him: ‘In my ward there is Master Li, over sixty, eight feet tall; everyone calls him the Mad Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: If you see the Duke of Pei, tell him: ‘In my ward there is Master Li, over sixty and eight feet tall; everyone calls him the Mad Scholar.

sentences.zh: 生自謂「我非狂生」。

translations.literal: The scholar himself says, “I am no mad scholar.”
translations.idiomatic: He himself says, “I am no mad scholar.”

sentences.zh: 』」騎士曰：「沛公不好儒，諸客冠儒冠來者，沛公輒解其冠，溲溺其中，與人言，常大罵，未可以儒生說也。

translations.literal: ’” The cavalryman said, “The Duke of Pei dislikes Ruists; when guests come wearing Ruist caps he snatches off the cap and urinates in it. When he speaks with men he often curses loudly—you cannot approach him as a Ru scholar.
translations.idiomatic: ’” The cavalryman said, “The Duke of Pei dislikes scholars; when guests arrive in scholar's caps he snatches off the cap and urinates in it. He talks in great oaths—you cannot win him over as a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 」酈生曰：「第言之。

translations.literal: ” Li Yi said, “Just tell him as I said.
translations.idiomatic: ” Li Yi said, “Tell him anyway.

sentences.zh: 」騎士從容言，如酈生所誡者。

translations.literal: ” The cavalryman spoke at leisure, just as Li Yi had instructed.
translations.idiomatic: ” The cavalryman spoke to him at his ease, exactly as Li Yi had directed.

sentences.zh: 沛公至高陽傳舍，使人召酈生。

translations.literal: The Duke of Pei reached the Gaoyang post-house and sent men to summon Li Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Pei reached the Gaoyang post-house, he sent for Li Yi.

sentences.zh: 酈生至，入謁。

translations.literal: Li Yi arrived and entered to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi came and was admitted to audience.

sentences.zh: 沛公方倨床使兩女子洗足，而見酈生。

translations.literal: The Duke of Pei was just then lounging on the bed having two women wash his feet as he received Li Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Pei was lounging on a couch having two women wash his feet when he received Li Yi.

sentences.zh: 酈生入，則長揖不拜，曰：「足下欲助秦攻諸侯乎？

translations.literal: Li Yi entered, made a long bow without the full prostration, and said, “Your lordship wishes to help Qin attack the allies?
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi entered, bowed with a long salute but did not prostrate himself, and said, “Do you mean to help Qin attack the allies?

sentences.zh: 且欲率諸侯破秦也？

translations.literal: Or do you wish to lead the allies to break Qin?
translations.idiomatic: Or do you mean to lead the allies to destroy Qin?

sentences.zh: 」沛公罵曰：「豎儒！

translations.literal: ” The Duke of Pei cursed, “Little Ru!
translations.idiomatic: ” The Duke of Pei swore, “You wretched scholar!

sentences.zh: 天下同苦秦久矣，故諸侯相率而攻秦，何謂助秦攻諸侯乎！

translations.literal: All under Heaven have long suffered under Qin; therefore the allies have joined to attack Qin—what do you mean by helping Qin attack the allies!
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm has long groaned under Qin; the allies have risen together against it—what do you mean by helping Qin attack the allies!

sentences.zh: 」酈生曰：「必聚徒合義兵誅無道秦，不宜倨見長者！

translations.literal: ” Li Yi said, “You must gather followers and unite righteous troops to execute lawless Qin—you ought not receive an elder in such a lounging posture!
translations.idiomatic: ” Li Yi said, “You must rally men and righteous armies to destroy lawless Qin—you should not receive an elder sprawled on your couch!

sentences.zh: 」於是沛公輟洗，起，攝衣，延酈生上坐，謝之。

translations.literal: ” The Duke of Pei then stopped the foot-washing, rose, straightened his clothes, invited Li Yi to the upper seat, and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Duke of Pei stopped the washing, rose, straightened his clothes, seated Li Yi in the place of honor, and apologized.

sentences.zh: 酈生因言六國從橫時。

translations.literal: Li Yi then spoke of the era when the Six States joined in horizontal alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi then discoursed on the age of the Six States' alliances.

sentences.zh: 沛公喜，賜酈生食，問曰：「計將安出？

translations.literal: The Duke of Pei was pleased, gave Li Yi food, and asked, “Where will the plan come forth?
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Pei was delighted, gave Li Yi a meal, and asked, “What is your plan?

sentences.zh: 」酈生曰：「足下起糾合之眾，收散亂之兵，不滿萬人；

translations.literal: ” Li Yi said, “Your lordship has raised a mustered crowd and gathered scattered troops—fewer than ten thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: ” Li Yi said, “You have raised a hastily gathered host and picked up scattered troops—fewer than ten thousand men;

sentences.zh: 欲以徑入強秦，此所謂探虎口者也。

translations.literal: yet you wish to plunge straight into powerful Qin—this is what they call reaching into a tiger's jaws.
translations.idiomatic: yet you mean to march straight into mighty Qin—that is what they call thrusting your hand into a tiger's maw.

sentences.zh: 夫陳留，天下之沖，四通五達之郊也，今其城中又多積粟。

translations.literal: Chenliu is the hub of all under Heaven, a crossroads where four ways meet and five connect; now within its walls grain is also piled high.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu is the hub of the realm, a crossroads where all roads meet, and its granaries are full.

sentences.zh: 臣善其令，請得使之令下足下。

translations.literal: Your servant is on good terms with its magistrate; I beg leave to have him surrender the city to your lordship.
translations.idiomatic: I am on good terms with its magistrate; let me have him surrender the city to you.

sentences.zh: 即不聽，足下引兵攻之，臣為內應。

translations.literal: If he will not listen, your lordship leads troops to attack and your servant will act as inner agent.
translations.idiomatic: If he refuses, you may attack, and I will act as your agent within the walls.

sentences.zh: 」於是遣酈生行，沛公引兵隨之，遂下陳留。

translations.literal: ” He then sent Li Yi on the mission; the Duke of Pei led his army after him and thereupon took Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent Li Yi ahead; the Duke of Pei followed with his army and took Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 號酈食其為廣野君。

translations.literal: He styled Li Yi Lord of Guangye.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Li Yi as Lord of Guangye.

sentences.zh: 酈生言其弟商。

translations.literal: Li Yi spoke of his younger brother Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi recommended his younger brother Shang.

sentences.zh: 時商聚少年得四千人，來屬沛公，沛公以為將，將陳留兵以從，酈生常為說客，使諸侯。

translations.literal: At that time Shang had gathered youths to four thousand men, came to submit to the Duke of Pei, who made him a general to lead Chenliu troops in attendance; Li Yi often served as envoy to the allies.
translations.idiomatic: Shang had by then gathered four thousand youths and came to join the Duke of Pei, who made him a general commanding Chenliu troops on campaign; Li Yi often served as envoy to the allied states.

sentences.zh: 三月，沛公攻開封，未拔。

translations.literal: In the third month the Duke of Pei attacked Kaifeng but did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Duke of Pei attacked Kaifeng but failed to capture it.

sentences.zh: 西與秦將楊熊會戰白馬，又戰曲遇東，大破之。

translations.literal: He went west and met Qin general Yang Xiong in battle at Baima; they fought again east of Quyu and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched west, met Qin general Yang Xiong at Baima, fought again east of Quyu, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 楊熊走之滎陽，二世使使者斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Yang Xiong fled to Xingyang; the Second Emperor sent an envoy to behead him and display the body as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong fled to Xingyang; the Second Emperor sent an envoy to execute him and expose the corpse as a warning.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，沛公南攻穎川，屠之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Duke of Pei attacked Yingchuan from the south and slaughtered it.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the Duke of Pei marched south against Yingchuan and put it to the sword.

sentences.zh: 因張良，遂略韓地。

translations.literal: Through Zhang Liang, he then overran Han territory.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Liang's help, he then overran Han territory.

sentences.zh: 時趙別將司馬卬方欲渡河入關。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao's detached general Sima Ang was just about to cross the river and enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao's detached general Sima Ang was about to cross the river and enter the passes.

sentences.zh: 沛公乃北攻平陰，絕河津南，戰洛陽東。

translations.literal: The Duke of Pei then attacked Pingyin in the north, severed the southern river crossings, and fought east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Pei then marched north against Pingyin, cut the southern river crossings, and fought east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 軍不利，南出轘轅。

translations.literal: The army fared poorly and went south out through Huanyuan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The army fared poorly and withdrew south through Huanyuan Pass.

sentences.zh: 張良引兵從沛公。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang led troops to follow the Duke of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang brought his troops to join the Duke of Pei.

sentences.zh: 沛公令韓王成留守陽翟，與良俱南。

translations.literal: The Duke of Pei ordered King Cheng of Han to hold Yangzhai and marched south with Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Pei left King Cheng of Han to hold Yangzhai and marched south with Liang.

sentences.zh: 六月，與南陽守齮戰犨東，破之，略南陽郡；

translations.literal: In the sixth month he fought Grand Administrator Zhi of Nanyang east of Bi, defeated him, and overran Nanyang commandery;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he fought Grand Administrator Zhi of Nanyang east of Bi, routed him, and overran Nanyang commandery;

sentences.zh: 南陽守走保城，守宛。

translations.literal: The grand administrator fled to hold a city and defended Wan.
translations.idiomatic: The grand administrator fled to a fortified city and held Wan.

sentences.zh: 沛公引兵過宛，西。

translations.literal: The Duke of Pei led his army past Wan, westward.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Pei marched past Wan and continued west.

sentences.zh: 張良諫曰：「沛公雖欲急入關，秦兵尚眾，距險。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang remonstrated, saying, “Though the Duke of Pei wishes urgently to enter the passes, Qin troops are still numerous and hold difficult terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang remonstrated: “Though you wish to hurry into the passes, Qin still has many troops holding difficult ground.

sentences.zh: 今不下宛，宛從後擊，強秦在前，此危道也。

translations.literal: If you do not take Wan now, Wan will strike from behind while powerful Qin is ahead—this is a perilous road.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not take Wan now, Wan will strike from behind while strong Qin blocks the way ahead—this is a deadly course.

sentences.zh: 」於是沛公乃夜引軍從他道還，偃旗幟，遲明，圍宛城三匝。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the Duke of Pei at night led his army back by another road, lowered banners and flags, and at dawn surrounded Wan city three times around.
translations.idiomatic: ” Thereupon the Duke of Pei by night led his army back by another route, lowered banners and flags, and at dawn had Wan surrounded three deep.

sentences.zh: 南陽守欲自剄，共舍人陳恢曰：「死未晚也。

translations.literal: The grand administrator of Nanyang wished to cut his own throat; his senior clerk Chen Hui said, “Death is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: The grand administrator of Nanyang was about to cut his throat when his senior clerk Chen Hui said, “It is not yet too late to die.

sentences.zh: 」乃逾城見沛公曰：「臣聞足下約先入咸陽者王之。

translations.literal: ” He then went over the wall to see the Duke of Pei and said, “Your servant has heard that under your agreement whoever enters Xianyang first is to be made king.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then went over the wall to see the Duke of Pei and said, “I have heard that by your agreement whoever enters Xianyang first shall be king.

sentences.zh: 今足下留守宛，宛郡縣連城數十，其吏民自以為降必死，故皆堅守乘城。

translations.literal: Now you have left Wan behind; Wan commandery has dozens of linked cities—its officials and people all believe that surrender means certain death, so all stoutly defend and mount the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Now you have left Wan behind. Nanyang has dozens of linked cities; its officials and people all believe surrender means death, so they hold the walls and fight on.

sentences.zh: 今足下盡日上攻，士死傷者必多。

translations.literal: If you assault all day, soldier deaths and wounds will surely be many.
translations.idiomatic: If you assault all day, your dead and wounded will surely be many.

sentences.zh: 引兵去宛，宛必隨足下後。

translations.literal: If you lead the army away from Wan, Wan will surely follow at your heels.
translations.idiomatic: If you march away from Wan, Wan will surely follow at your heels.

sentences.zh: 足下前則失咸陽之約，後有強宛之患。

translations.literal: Ahead you fail the Xianyang agreement; behind you have the trouble of powerful Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Ahead you break the Xianyang pact; behind you face the menace of strong Wan.

sentences.zh: 為足下計，莫若約降，封其守；

translations.literal: For your planning, nothing is better than agreeing to surrender and enfeoffing the defender;
translations.idiomatic: For your own sake, nothing is better than accepting surrender and enfeoffing the defender;

sentences.zh: 因使止守，引其甲卒與之西。

translations.literal: then have him continue to hold the place and lead his armored troops west with you.
translations.idiomatic: then have him keep holding the city and lead his armored troops west with you.

sentences.zh: 諸城未下者，聞聲爭開門而待足下，足下通行無所累。

translations.literal: Cities not yet taken, hearing the news, will compete to open their gates and await you—you will pass without hindrance.
translations.idiomatic: Cities not yet taken will hear the news and vie to open their gates for you; you will march on without hindrance.

sentences.zh: 」沛公曰：「善！

translations.literal: ” The Duke of Pei said, “Good!
translations.idiomatic: ” The Duke of Pei said, “Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」秋，七月，南陽守齮降，封為殷侯，封陳恢千戶。

translations.literal: ” In autumn, the seventh month, Grand Administrator Zhi of Nanyang surrendered; he was enfeoffed as Marquis Yin; Chen Hui was given a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: ” In autumn, the seventh month, Grand Administrator Zhi of Nanyang surrendered; he was made Marquis Yin, and Chen Hui received a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 引兵西，無不下者。

translations.literal: He led his army west; none he met failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He marched west, and every place he reached submitted.

sentences.zh: 至丹水，高武侯鰓、襄侯王陵降。

translations.literal: Reaching Dan River, Marquis Wu of Gaoyang E and Marquis Xiang Wang Ling surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Dan River, Marquis Wu of Gaoyang E and Marquis Xiang Wang Ling surrendered.

sentences.zh: 還攻胡陽，遇番君別將梅鋗，與偕攻析、酈，皆降。

translations.literal: He turned to attack Huyang, met Fan Jun's detached general Mei Xuan, and together attacked Xi and Li—all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back to attack Huyang, met Fan Jun's detached general Mei Xuan, and together they attacked Xi and Li—both surrendered.

sentences.zh: 所過亡得鹵掠，秦民皆喜。

translations.literal: Where they passed none could snatch plunder; the common people of Qin were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Where they passed no one could plunder; the people of Qin were all pleased.

sentences.zh: 7王離軍既沒，章邯軍棘原，項羽軍漳南，相持未戰。

translations.literal: 7 Wang Li's army having been destroyed, Zhang Han's army was at Jiyuan, Xiang Yu's army south of the Zhang, facing each other without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: 7 After Wang Li's army was destroyed, Zhang Han camped at Jiyuan and Xiang Yu south of the Zhang—they faced each other but did not fight.

sentences.zh: 秦軍數卻，二世使人讓章邯。

translations.literal: The Qin army repeatedly fell back; the Second Emperor sent men to reproach Zhang Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin army kept falling back; the Second Emperor sent men to rebuke Zhang Han.

sentences.zh: 章邯恐，使長史欣請事。

translations.literal: Zhang Han was afraid and sent Chief Clerk Xin to report on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han was afraid and sent Chief Clerk Xin to report to court.

sentences.zh: 至咸陽，留司馬門三日，趙高不見，有不信之心。

translations.literal: Arriving at Xianyang, he waited three days at the Sima Gate; Zhao Gao would not see him—he had thoughts of distrust.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Xianyang, he waited three days at the Sima Gate; Zhao Gao would not see him, and he began to doubt.

sentences.zh: 長史欣恐，還走其軍，不敢出故道。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Xin was afraid, returned running to his army, and did not dare go out by the old road.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Xin was afraid, fled back to the army, and did not dare return by the old road.

sentences.zh: 趙高果使人追之，不及。

translations.literal: Zhao Gao indeed sent men to pursue him but did not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao did send men in pursuit but could not overtake him.

sentences.zh: 欣至軍，報曰：「趙高用事於中，下無可為者。

translations.literal: Xin reached the army and reported, saying, “Zhao Gao holds power within; below there is nothing that can be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin reached the army he reported: “Zhao Gao holds power at court; below there is nothing we can do.

sentences.zh: 今戰能勝，高必疾妒吾功，不能勝，不免於死。

translations.literal: If we fight and can win, Gao will surely be jealous of our merit; if we cannot win, we cannot escape death.
translations.idiomatic: If we fight and win, Gao will surely envy our merit; if we lose, we cannot escape death.

sentences.zh: 願將軍孰計之！

translations.literal: The general wishes you to weigh this carefully!
translations.idiomatic: I beg the general to weigh this carefully!

sentences.zh: 」陳餘亦遺章邯書曰：「白起為秦將，南征鄢郢，北坑馬服，攻城略地，不可勝計，而竟賜死。

translations.literal: ” Chen Yu also sent Zhang Han a letter, saying, “Bai Qi was Qin's general—south he campaigned against Yan and Ying, north he buried the Lord of Ma-fu, besieged cities and seized territory beyond counting, yet in the end was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chen Yu also wrote Zhang Han: “Bai Qi was Qin's general—south he took Yan and Ying, north he destroyed the Lord of Ma-fu, besieged cities and seized land beyond counting, yet in the end was put to death.

sentences.zh: 蒙恬為秦將，北逐戎人，開榆中地數千里，竟斬陽周。

translations.literal: Meng Tian was Qin's general—north he drove off the Rong, opened several thousand li of Yuzhong territory, yet in the end was beheaded at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Tian was Qin's general—north he drove off the Rong and opened several thousand li in Yuzhong, yet in the end was executed at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 功多，秦不能盡封，因以法誅之。

translations.literal: Merit was great; Qin could not enfeoff them all, so executed them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Their merit was too great for Qin to reward fully, so they were killed under the law.

sentences.zh: 今將軍為秦將三歲矣，所亡失以十萬數，而諸侯並起滋益多。

translations.literal: Now the general has been Qin's general three years; losses number in the tens of thousands, while the allies rise together ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: You have been Qin's general three years; your losses run into the tens of thousands, while the allies rise ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 彼趙高素諛日久，今事急，亦恐二世誅之，故欲以法誅將軍以塞責，使人更代將軍以脫其禍。

translations.literal: That Zhao Gao has long been a flatterer; now affairs are urgent and he also fears the Second Emperor will execute him—so he wishes to execute the general by law to answer for blame and send someone to replace the general and escape his own disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao has long flattered the throne; now in crisis he fears the Second Emperor will kill him—so he means to kill you under the law to answer for failures and send another general in your place to save himself.

sentences.zh: 夫將軍居外久，多內郤，有功亦誅，無功亦誅。

translations.literal: The general has long been abroad with many inner grievances—merit brings execution, no merit also brings execution.
translations.idiomatic: You have long been abroad with many enemies at court—win and you are killed, lose and you are killed.

sentences.zh: 且天之亡秦，無愚智皆知之。

translations.literal: Moreover Heaven is destroying Qin—none, foolish or wise, fails to know it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Heaven is destroying Qin—fool and sage alike know it.

sentences.zh: 今將軍內不能直諫，外為亡國將，孤特獨立而欲常存，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Now the general within cannot remonstrate uprightly, without is a general of a perishing state—standing alone and wishing to endure forever—is it not pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: Now you cannot remonstrate at court, without you are a general of a dying state—standing alone yet hoping to survive forever. Is it not pitiful!

sentences.zh: 將軍何不還兵與諸侯為從，約共攻秦，分王其地，南面稱孤！

translations.literal: Why does the general not turn the army and join the allies in alliance, agree to attack Qin together, divide Qin territory into kingships, and face south calling himself isolated king!
translations.idiomatic: Why not turn your army, join the allies, agree to attack Qin together, divide its land into kingdoms, and face south as a king in your own right!

sentences.zh: 此孰與身伏鈇質、妻子為戮乎？

translations.literal: Which is better than personally laying your body on the axe-block and wife and children being slaughtered?
translations.idiomatic: Which is better than laying your neck on the block and seeing your wife and children slaughtered?

sentences.zh: 章邯狐疑，陰使候始成使項羽，欲約。

translations.literal: Zhang Han hesitated; secretly he sent scout Shi Cheng to Xiang Yu, wishing to negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han wavered and secretly sent scout Shi Cheng to Xiang Yu to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 約未成，項羽使蒲將日夜引兵度三戶，軍漳南，與秦軍戰，再破之。

translations.literal: The pact was not concluded; Xiang Yu sent General Pu day and night to lead troops across Sanhu, camp south of the Zhang, fight the Qin army, and twice defeat it.
translations.idiomatic: Before the pact was made, Xiang Yu sent General Pu day and night to lead troops across Sanhu, camp south of the Zhang, fight the Qin army, and defeat it twice.

sentences.zh: 項羽悉引兵擊秦軍汙水上，大破之。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu then led all his troops to strike the Qin army on the Wushui and routed it greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu then brought his whole army against the Qin force on the Wushui and crushed it.

sentences.zh: 章邯使人見項羽，欲約。

translations.literal: Zhang Han sent men to see Xiang Yu and wished to negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han sent envoys to Xiang Yu to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 項羽召軍吏謀曰：「糧少，欲聽其約。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu summoned army officers to counsel, saying, “Grain is scarce; I wish to accept their pact.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu called his officers to counsel and said, “Our grain is low; I wish to accept their terms.

sentences.zh: 」軍吏皆曰：「善。

translations.literal: ” The army officers all said, “Good.
translations.idiomatic: ” The officers all said, “Good.

sentences.zh: 」項羽乃與期洹水殷虛上。

translations.literal: ” Xiang Yu then set a date at Yin Xu on the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xiang Yu then set a meeting at Yin Xu on the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 已盟，章邯見項羽而流涕，為言趙高。

translations.literal: After the pact, Zhang Han saw Xiang Yu and wept, speaking of Zhao Gao.
translations.idiomatic: After the pact was sworn, Zhang Han met Xiang Yu in tears and spoke of Zhao Gao.

sentences.zh: 項羽乃立章邯為雍王，置楚軍中，使長史欣為上將軍，將秦軍為前行。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu then established Zhang Han as King of Yong, placed him in the Chu army, made Chief Clerk Xin supreme general, and had him lead the Qin army as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu then made Zhang Han King of Yong, kept him with the Chu army, appointed Chief Clerk Xin supreme general, and set him to lead the Qin troops as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 瑕丘申陽下河南，引兵從項羽。

translations.literal: Shen Yang of Xiaqiu came down to Henan and led troops to follow Xiang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yang of Xiaqiu came down into Henan and led his troops to follow Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 8初，中丞相趙高欲專秦權，恐群臣不聽，乃先設驗，持鹿獻於二世曰：「馬也。

translations.literal: 8 At first Grand Minister Zhao Gao wished to monopolize Qin power, feared the ministers would not heed him, so first set a test—he held a deer and presented it to the Second Emperor, saying, “A horse.
translations.idiomatic: 8 At first Grand Minister Zhao Gao wished to monopolize Qin's power and feared the ministers would not obey him, so he first set a test: he brought a deer and presented it to the Second Emperor, saying, “A horse.

sentences.zh: 」二世笑曰：「丞相誤邪，謂鹿為馬！

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor laughed and said, “Has the chancellor erred, calling a deer a horse!
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor laughed and said, “Has the chancellor made a mistake, calling a deer a horse!

sentences.zh: 」問左右，左右或默，或言馬以阿順趙高，或言鹿者。

translations.literal: ” He asked those at his side; some were silent, some said horse to flatter Zhao Gao, some said deer.
translations.idiomatic: ” He asked those beside him; some were silent, some said horse to flatter Zhao Gao, and some said deer.

sentences.zh: 高因陰中諸言鹿者以法。

translations.literal: Gao then secretly struck down by law all who said deer.
translations.idiomatic: Gao then secretly punished by law all who had said deer.

sentences.zh: 後群臣皆畏高，莫敢言其過。

translations.literal: Afterward the ministers all feared Gao; none dared speak of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the ministers all feared Gao and none dared speak of his faults.

sentences.zh: 高前數言「關東盜無能為也」，及項羽虜王離等，而章邯等軍數敗，上書請益助。

translations.literal: Gao had earlier repeatedly said, “The bandits east of the passes can accomplish nothing”—when Xiang Yu captured Wang Li and the rest and Zhang Han's army was repeatedly defeated, he memorialized requesting more aid.
translations.idiomatic: Gao had repeatedly said, “The rebels east of the passes can do nothing”—yet when Xiang Yu captured Wang Li and Zhang Han's army was beaten again and again, he memorialized asking for more reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 自關以東，大抵盡畔秦吏，應諸侯，諸侯鹹率其眾西鄉。

translations.literal: East of the passes, nearly all turned from Qin officials and answered the allies; the allies all led their masses westward.
translations.idiomatic: East of the passes nearly all Qin officials rebelled and answered the allies, and the allies all led their hosts west.

sentences.zh: 八月，沛公將數萬人攻武關，屠之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Duke of Pei with tens of thousands of men attacked Wuguan and slaughtered it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Duke of Pei led tens of thousands against Wuguan and put it to the sword.

sentences.zh: 高恐二世怒，誅及其身，乃謝病，不朝見。

translations.literal: Gao feared the Second Emperor's anger would reach execution upon his person, so pleaded illness and did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Gao feared the Second Emperor's wrath would reach him, pleaded illness, and stopped attending court.

sentences.zh: 二世夢白虎嚙其左驂馬，殺之，心不樂，怪問占夢。

translations.literal: The Second Emperor dreamed a white tiger bit his left outer horse and killed it; his heart was uneasy; suspiciously he asked the dream interpreter.
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor dreamed a white tiger bit and killed his left outer horse; uneasy at heart, he asked the dream interpreter what it meant.

sentences.zh: 卜曰：「涇水為祟。

translations.literal: Divination said, “The Jing River is the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Divination said, “The Jing River is the source of harm.

sentences.zh: 」二世乃齋於望夷宮，欲祠涇水，沈四白馬。

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor then fasted at Wangyi Palace, wished to sacrifice to the Jing River, and sank four white horses.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor then fasted at Wangyi Palace, prepared to sacrifice to the Jing River, and sank four white horses.

sentences.zh: 使使責讓高以盜賊事。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to reproach Gao regarding the rebel bandit affair.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to rebuke Gao over the rebel troubles.

sentences.zh: 高懼，乃陰與其婿咸陽令閻樂及弟趙成謀曰：「上不聽諫。

translations.literal: Gao was afraid and secretly plotted with his son-in-law Lord of Xianyang Yan Le and his younger brother Zhao Cheng, saying, “The emperor above will not heed remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was afraid and secretly plotted with his son-in-law, the magistrate of Xianyang Yan Le, and his younger brother Zhao Cheng, saying, “The emperor will not heed remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 今事急，欲歸禍於吾。

translations.literal: Now affairs are urgent and he wishes to shift blame onto us.
translations.idiomatic: Now that things are desperate, he means to shift the blame onto us.

sentences.zh: 吾欲易置上，更立子嬰。

translations.literal: We wish to replace the emperor above and install Ziying instead.
translations.idiomatic: We mean to replace the emperor and set up Ziying instead.

sentences.zh: 子嬰仁儉，百姓皆載其言。

translations.literal: Ziying is benevolent and frugal; the common people all praise his words.
translations.idiomatic: Ziying is humane and frugal, and the people all praise him.

sentences.zh: 」乃使郎中令為內應，詐為有大賊，令樂召吏發兵追，劫樂母置高舍。

translations.literal: ” He then had the Court Commandant as inner agent, falsely claimed great bandits, ordered Le to summon officers and dispatch troops in pursuit, and seized Le's mother and placed her at Gao's residence.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had the Court Commandant act as inside agent, pretended there were great bandits, ordered Le to summon officers and raise troops in pursuit, and seized Le's mother and held her at Gao's house.

sentences.zh: 遣樂將吏卒千餘人至望夷宮殿門，縛衛令僕射，曰：「賊入此，何不止？

translations.literal: He sent Le leading officers and soldiers more than a thousand to Wangyi Palace gate, bound the Guard Commandant's Master of Chariots, and said, “Bandits entered here—why did you not stop them?
translations.idiomatic: He sent Le with more than a thousand officers and soldiers to the gate of Wangyi Palace, bound the Guard Commandant's Master of Chariots, and said, “Bandits entered here—why did you not stop them?

sentences.zh: 」衛令曰：「周廬設卒甚謹，安得賊敢入宮！

translations.literal: ” The Guard Commandant said, “The encircling palisades post guards with great care—how could bandits dare enter the palace!
translations.idiomatic: ” The Guard Commandant said, “The encircling guards are posted with great care—how could bandits dare enter the palace!

sentences.zh: 」樂遂斬衛令，直將吏入，行射郎、宦者。

translations.literal: ” Le then beheaded the Guard Commandant, led officers and soldiers straight in, and went shooting Gentlemen of the Palace and eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: ” Le then beheaded the Guard Commandant, led his officers straight in, and shot down palace gentlemen and eunuchs as he went.

sentences.zh: 郎、宦者大驚，或走，或格。

translations.literal: The Gentlemen and eunuchs were greatly alarmed—some fled, some resisted.
translations.idiomatic: The gentlemen and eunuchs were terrified—some fled, some fought back.

sentences.zh: 格者輒死，死者數十人。

translations.literal: Those who resisted were immediately killed; the dead numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Those who resisted were killed on the spot; several tens died.

sentences.zh: 郎中令與樂俱入，射上幄坐幃。

translations.literal: The Court Commandant entered together with Le and shot at the emperor's curtain-enclosed seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Court Commandant entered with Le and shot at the emperor behind his curtain.

sentences.zh: 二世怒，召左右，左右皆惶擾不鬥。

translations.literal: The Second Emperor was angry and summoned those at his side; those at his side were all alarmed and disturbed and would not fight.
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor was furious and called his attendants, but they were all panicked and would not fight.

sentences.zh: 旁有宦者一人侍，不敢去。

translations.literal: At his side one eunuch attended and did not dare leave.
translations.idiomatic: One eunuch still attended at his side and did not dare leave.

sentences.zh: 二世入內，謂曰：「公何不早告我，乃至於此！

translations.literal: The Second Emperor went inside and said to him, “Why did you not tell me early—it has come to this!
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor went inside and said to him, “Why did you not tell me sooner—it has come to this!

sentences.zh: 」宦者曰：「臣不敢言，故得全。

translations.literal: ” The eunuch said, “Your servant did not dare speak—therefore I was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: ” The eunuch said, “I did not dare speak—that is why I am still alive.

sentences.zh: 使臣早言，皆已誅，安得至今！

translations.literal: Had your servant spoken early, all would already have been executed—how could I reach today!
translations.idiomatic: Had I spoken earlier, I would already have been killed—how could I be here today!

sentences.zh: 」閻樂前即二世，數曰：「足下驕恣，誅殺無道，天下共畔足下。

translations.literal: ” Yan Le stepped forward to approach the Second Emperor and enumerated, saying, “Your Grace is arrogant and willful, executes without principle—all under Heaven together rebels against Your Grace.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yan Le stepped forward to the Second Emperor and said, “Your Grace is arrogant and lawless in killing; all under Heaven rebels against you.

sentences.zh: 足下其自為計！

translations.literal: Your Grace should plan for yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Plan for yourself!

sentences.zh: 」二世曰：「丞相可得見否？

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor said, “Can I see the chancellor?
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor said, “May I see the chancellor?

sentences.zh: 」樂曰：「不可！

translations.literal: ” Le said, “No!
translations.idiomatic: ” Le said, “No!

sentences.zh: 」二世曰：「吾願得一郡為王。

translations.literal: ” The Second Emperor said, “I wish to have one commandery and be king.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Second Emperor said, “I wish to have one commandery and be king.

sentences.zh: 」弗許。

translations.literal: ” This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: ” This was refused.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「願為萬戶侯。

translations.literal: Again he said, “I wish to be a marquis of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Again he said, “I wish to be a marquis of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 」弗許。

translations.literal: ” This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: ” This too was refused.

sentences.zh: 曰：「願與妻子為黔首，比諸公子。

translations.literal: He said, “I wish to be a black-headed commoner with wife and children, like the other imperial sons.
translations.idiomatic: He said, “I wish to live as a commoner with my wife and children, like the other imperial sons.

sentences.zh: 」閻樂曰：「臣受命於丞相，為天下誅足下。

translations.literal: ” Yan Le said, “Your servant received orders from the chancellor to execute Your Grace for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yan Le said, “I have orders from the chancellor to execute you on behalf of all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 足下雖多言，臣不敢報！

translations.literal: Though Your Grace speaks much, your servant dares not report it!
translations.idiomatic: Though you speak much, I dare not report it!

sentences.zh: 」麾其兵進。

translations.literal: ” He waved his troops forward.
translations.idiomatic: ” He waved his troops forward.

sentences.zh: 二世自殺。

translations.literal: The Second Emperor killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor killed himself.

sentences.zh: 閻樂歸報趙高。

translations.literal: Yan Le returned and reported to Zhao Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Le returned and reported to Zhao Gao.

sentences.zh: 趙高乃悉召諸大臣、公子，告以誅二世之狀，曰：「秦故王國，始皇君天下，故稱帝。

translations.literal: Zhao Gao then summoned all the great ministers and royal sons, informed them of how the Second Emperor had been executed, and said, “Qin was originally a feudal kingdom; the First Emperor ruled all under Heaven, therefore he was called Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao then summoned all the great ministers and princes, told them how the Second Emperor had been killed, and said, “Qin was originally a feudal kingdom; the First Emperor ruled the realm, and therefore was called Emperor.

sentences.zh: 今六國復自立，秦地益小，乃以空名為帝，不可。

translations.literal: Now the Six States have risen again and established themselves; Qin territory grows ever smaller—to hold the empty title of Emperor will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Six States have risen again and Qin territory grows ever smaller—to hold the empty title of Emperor will not do.

sentences.zh: 宜為王如故，便。

translations.literal: It is fitting to be king as of old—that is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to be king as before—that is best.

sentences.zh: 」乃立子嬰為秦王。

translations.literal: ” He then established Ziying as King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then made Ziying King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 以黔首葬二世社南宜春苑中。

translations.literal: He buried the Second Emperor as a commoner south of the altar in the Yichun Garden.
translations.idiomatic: He buried the Second Emperor as a commoner south of the altar in the Yichun Garden.

sentences.zh: 九月，趙高令子嬰齋戒，當廟見，受玉璽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Zhao Gao ordered Ziying to purify himself; when he should appear at the ancestral temple he was to receive the jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zhao Gao ordered Ziying to fast and purify himself; he was to appear at the ancestral temple and receive the jade seal.

sentences.zh: 齋五日。

translations.literal: He fasted for five days.
translations.idiomatic: He fasted for five days.

sentences.zh: 子嬰與其子二人謀曰：「丞相高殺二世望夷宮，恐群臣誅之，乃佯以義立我。

translations.literal: Ziying and his two sons plotted, saying, “Chancellor Gao killed the Second Emperor at Wangyi Palace, fearing the ministers would execute him; he therefore pretended to establish me out of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Ziying and his two sons plotted, saying, “Chancellor Gao killed the Second Emperor at Wangyi Palace, fearing the ministers would execute him; he therefore pretended to establish me out of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 我聞趙高乃與楚約，滅秦宗室而分王關中。

translations.literal: I hear Zhao Gao has made a pact with Chu to destroy the Qin imperial clan and divide Guanzhong into separate kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Zhao Gao has made a pact with Chu to destroy the Qin imperial clan and divide Guanzhong into separate kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 今使我齋、見廟，此欲因廟中殺我。

translations.literal: Now he makes me fast and appear at the temple—he intends to kill me in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Now he makes me fast and appear at the temple—he intends to kill me there.

sentences.zh: 我稱病不行，丞相必自來，來則殺之。

translations.literal: If I claim illness and do not go, the chancellor will surely come in person; when he comes, we kill him.
translations.idiomatic: If I claim illness and do not go, the chancellor will surely come in person; when he comes, we kill him.

sentences.zh: 」高使人請子嬰數輩，子嬰不行。

translations.literal: ” Gao sent men to summon Ziying several times; Ziying did not go.
translations.idiomatic: ” Gao sent men to summon Ziying several times; Ziying did not go.

sentences.zh: 高果自往，曰：「宗廟重事，王奈何不行？

translations.literal: Gao did indeed come in person and said, “The ancestral temple affairs are weighty—why does the king not go?
translations.idiomatic: Gao did indeed come in person and said, “Affairs of the ancestral temple are weighty—why does Your Majesty not go?

sentences.zh: 」子嬰遂刺殺高於齋宮，三族高家以徇。

translations.literal: ” Ziying then stabbed and killed Gao in the fasting palace; the three clans of Gao's family were exterminated and displayed as warning.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ziying then stabbed and killed Gao in the fasting palace; Gao's three clans were exterminated and exposed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 遣將兵距嶢關，沛公欲擊之。

translations.literal: He sent a general with troops to hold Yao Pass; the Duke of Pei wished to attack.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops to hold Yao Pass; the Duke of Pei wished to attack.

sentences.zh: 張良曰：「秦兵尚強，未可輕。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang said, “Qin troops are still strong—they must not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang said, “Qin troops are still strong—they must not be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 願先遣人益張旗幟於山上為疑兵，使酈食其、陸賈往說秦將，啖以利。

translations.literal: I beg first to send men to multiply banners on the mountains as feigned troops, and send Li Yiji and Lu Jia to persuade the Qin general, enticing him with profit.
translations.idiomatic: I beg first to send men to multiply banners on the mountains as decoys, and send Li Yiji and Lu Jia to persuade the Qin general, tempting him with gain.

sentences.zh: 」秦將果欲連和，沛公欲許之。

translations.literal: ” The Qin general indeed wished to join in alliance; the Duke of Pei wished to agree.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Qin general indeed wished to ally; the Duke of Pei wished to agree.

sentences.zh: 張良曰：「此獨其將欲叛，恐其士卒不從；

translations.literal: Zhang Liang said, “This is only the general wishing to rebel—I fear his soldiers will not follow;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang said, “Only the general wishes to rebel—I fear his soldiers will not follow;

sentences.zh: 不如因其懈怠擊之。

translations.literal: better to strike them while they are slack.
translations.idiomatic: better to strike them while they are slack.

sentences.zh: 」沛公引兵繞嶢關，逾蕢山，擊秦軍，大破之藍田南。

translations.literal: ” The Duke of Pei led his army around Yao Pass, crossed Zhi Mountain, struck the Qin army, and routed them greatly south of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Duke of Pei led his army around Yao Pass, crossed Zhi Mountain, attacked the Qin army, and routed them south of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 遂至藍田，又戰其北，秦兵大敗。

translations.literal: He then reached Lantian and fought again north of it; the Qin army was routed utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He then reached Lantian and fought again to the north; the Qin army was routed utterly.
